items.title: Power sector fix ‘ongoing work’, APC-PCC counters criticisms of Tinubu’s 2023 pledge
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council APC-PCC has said that fixing Nigeria’s electricity sector is “ongoing work”, as it countered criticisms of President Bola Tinubu’s 2023 pledge to end estimated billing and deliver stable power. In a statement on Sunday, the Spokesperson of the APC-PCC, Dele Alake, said recent public commentary had reproduced the campaign promise without its closing qualification. Speaking to members of the Organised Private Sector (OPS) in Lagos ahead of the 2023 general elections, Tinubu, then the APC candidate, had reportedly said: “Whichever way, by all means necessary, you will have electricity, and you will not pay for estimated bills anymore. A promise made will be a promise kept. If I don’t keep the promise and I come for a second term, don’t vote for me, unless I give you adequate reasons why I couldn’t deliver.” Alake said the commentary left out the final part, that “should he fall short, he would owe Nigerians an adequate explanation before seeking their support for a second term.” He argued that “a fair assessment of the pledge should consider the full statement alongside the administration’s record since 2023,” measured “against measurable improvements in electricity supply, metering, infrastructure and market stability.” “While fixing the power sector crisis remains unfinished, the President is working consistently to deliver on his promise to Nigerians, and his commitment to face the challenges head-on has never diminished,” the statement said. The APC-PCC said Tinubu signed the Electricity Act, 2023 on June 9, within two weeks of taking office. According to the statement, the law liberalised and deregulated the power sector and moved it away from the Exclusive List, so that states can take part in power generation, distribution and transmission. It said Lagos, Enugu, Abia, Ekiti, Oyo, Kaduna and Niger states have started using the law to set up their own electricity regulatory agencies and attract private capital. On debts, the campaign council said Tinubu “took on the over N6 trillion legacy debt that had accumulated from 2015 to 2025.” It added that the administration created a N4 trillion bond programme to settle verified legacy debts owed to 21 power generation companies (Gencos) and gas companies (Gascos). The first and second tranches of the programme have raised over N1.2 trillion, the statement said. It added that the effect was becoming evident in the ability of Gencos to invest in upgrading their plants. “Just a few days ago, Geregu Power Plc announced investments in new Power Transformers to enhance operations at the Geregu 1 Power Plant. Other firms are making similar investments,” it said. On metering, the statement said Tinubu started a Presidential Metering Initiative to close a gap of over seven million meters. It said over 1.5 million customers had been metered under the initiative in the last three years. The APC-PCC added that the Rural Electrification Agency has connected universities, hospitals and rural communities to solar power. It said the government has also unveiled plans to modernise the Osogbo Grid Control Centre, which it said was built over 60 years ago, and to build an East-West super grid. On transmission, the council said Tinubu reviewed the Presidential Power Initiative (PPI), which was started by the late President Muhammadu Buhari, and signed an Acceleration Agreement in December 2023 with the German partners. It said the Federal Executive Council (FEC) approved the contract for the first batch of five Transmission Company of Nigeria (TCN) substations in key load centres by December 2024. These projects, it said, “are now being completed and will be commissioned before the end of the administration’s first term.” In June 2026, the statement added, FEC approved the contract for a second batch, covering eight new substations and the upgrade of four existing ones. “Power project implementation requires equipment that is a long-lead item and thus cannot be achieved overnight,” the statement said. On tariffs, Alake said Tinubu “significantly aligned the tariffs to cost to restore liquidity to the electricity market” and put in place a system to protect low-income households. The creation of Service Bands with different tariffs, he said, was a first step to improve the financial viability of distribution companies and cash flow in the sector. It also reduced the government’s financial burden from tariff subsidies. “The administration will continue to explore ways to improve the commercial situation of the power sector while protecting access to electricity for the less privileged in society,” the statement said. The campaign council declared: “Fixing the electricity market and power sector is ongoing work.” “President Tinubu has not deviated an inch from his commitment. As he seeks Nigerians’ mandate for a second term in office, he will proudly present his scorecard in the power sector and clearly tell Nigerians what remains to be done,” Alake said. items.title: Climate diplomacy meets frontline reality: AGN opens COP31 strategy session amid urgent El Niño warnings
items.description: The African Group of Negotiators on Climate Change (AGN) has opened a crucial two-day strategy meeting in Antalya, Türkiye, to prepare for the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31). The urgency of their negotiations is underscored by alarming real-world climate advisories emerging across the African continent. Convening from November 1 to 2, the negotiating body seeks to unify Africa’s voice ahead of global climate talks, a task rendered vital by newly confirmed meteorological data indicating severe climate shocks ahead. Concurrently, the Ghana Meteorological Agency (GMet) has issued an urgent advisory confirming that a very strong El Niño event is developing in the Pacific Ocean and will heavily influence West African weather into the first half of 2027. The convergence of high-level climate diplomacy in Türkiye and frontline weather advisories in Ghana highlights an imperative message for COP31: international climate governance must deliver concrete, actionable outcomes that build resilience and safeguard vulnerable communities against devastating climate impacts. The AGN plays a central role in coordinating the positions of African nations and representing the continent’s common interests within the United Nations climate process. The strategy meeting in Antalya brings negotiators together to consolidate preparations, strengthen continental coordination, and ensure a unified stance at COP31 and subsequent international forums. Opening the session, AGN Chair Nana Dr. Antwi-Boasiako Amoah stressed that unity, cooperation, and collective commitment are essential to elevating Africa’s voice on the global stage. He commended members for their steadfast dedication despite demanding schedules and competing professional responsibilities. “The spirit of teamwork demonstrated by members will be crucial in ensuring a coordinated approach to the negotiations and securing outcomes that reflect Africa’s priorities and development needs,” emphasized Dr. Amoah, urging negotiators to maintain their shared sense of purpose. The Antalya consultations aim to reinforce the group’s collective climate diplomacy and build institutional capacity to secure international agreements focused on adaptation funding, developmental equity, and robust support for climate-vulnerable populations. The Looming Climate Shock: GMet Confirms Intensifying El Niño While diplomatic strategies take shape in Türkiye, operational advisories from West Africa illustrate the escalating environmental pressures facing African nations. In an official advisory issued on October 29, 2026, the Ghana Meteorological Agency (GMet) confirmed that a very strong El Niño event is intensifying in the Pacific Ocean. Joint observations from GMet and leading international climate centers—including the US National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), the International Research Institute for Climate and Society (IRI), and the World Meteorological Organization (WMO)—indicate that the event will peak between now and January 2027 before gradually weakening through the first half of 2027. Historical experience demonstrates Ghana’s high vulnerability to El Niño-induced rainfall variability. Previous very strong events in 1982/83, 1997/98, and 2015/16, as well as the moderate event of 2023/24, severely impacted key economic and social sectors across the country: Agricultural Production: Severe rainfall deficits disrupted planting cycles, reduced crop yields, and threatened food security. Water Resources and Hydroelectric Power: Extended dry spells depleted reservoir levels, constraining water availability and hydroelectric power generation. Public Health: Extended heat and dry dust transport created environmental conditions conducive to disease outbreaks. The GMet advisory for 2027 underscores that the consequences of extreme weather fall most heavily on vulnerable populations. Protecting these communities requires translating meteorological forecasts into targeted mitigation measures across key sectors, including health, water resources, the agricultural sector and food security. The parallel developments in Antalya and West Africa illustrate why global climate negotiations cannot take place in a vacuum. As AGN negotiators work to shape Africa’s strategic stance ahead of COP31, the realities on the ground in Ghana demonstrate that climate policy must ultimately serve to shield vulnerable communities from environmental disaster. By coupling strong, unified diplomatic advocacy with robust local disaster preparedness, African nations can better protect lives, safeguard food and energy systems, and build enduring resilience against an increasingly volatile climate.

items.title: UBIDS halts new programmes as Parliament probes accreditation and staffing crisis
items.description: The University of Business and Integrated Development Studies (UBIDS) has suspended the rollout of all new academic programmes as the Parliamentary Committee on Education investigates a severe accreditation backlog, critical staffing shortages and mounting infrastructure debts. The institution’s growing issues were laid bare during a recent parliamentary oversight visit, where university management faced intense scrutiny over the operational realities of transitioning to full autonomy. After its former parent university declined to process its accreditations, UBIDS was forced to independently repackage and submit a staggering 177 programmes for approval. The Vice-Chairman of the Education Committee, Joseph Kwame Kumah, warned that running unaccredited programmes alongside severe faculty shortages poses a critical risk to students, pointing to past precedents where institutions were forced to “teach out” and discontinue failing programmes. During the session, the Member of Parliament for Offinso North, Dr Fred Kyei Asamoah, led a sweeping inquiry into the university’s strategic and financial viability. Dr Asamoah questioned how an institution with just 227 lecturers could sustain 177 programmes, especially when its 1,898 weekend master’s students vastly outnumbered its 356 regular students. He also heavily scrutinised the feasibility of launching a medical school by 2027 without a dedicated teaching hospital or sufficient faculty, and demanded accountability for how a GH¢10 million seed fund was utilised, alongside concerns over a projected tenfold increase in casual staff costs. In a robust defence, the UBIDS Vice-Chancellor, Prof. Emmanuel Kanchebe Derbile, revealed that the university’s financial and infrastructural woes are deeply tied to external constraints. He disclosed that the government still owes GH¢114 million for land acquisition, a lingering debt that has severely hampered campus development. Currently, a planned 600-bed facility would accommodate only 6 per cent of the university’s roughly 10,000-student population. Addressing the staffing crisis, the Vice-Chancellor noted that the university lost 55 critical staff members to the University for Development Studies (UDS) during the transition to autonomy—a loss he attributed to poor transfer protocols. However, management has recently secured approval from the Ghana Tertiary Education Commission (GTEC) to recruit new assistant lecturers to bridge the gap. The parliamentary session also spotlighted a stark gender disparity at the postgraduate level, with female enrolment declining from 52 per cent in diploma programmes to 27 per cent at the master’s level, and just 15 per cent at the PhD level. In response, the Vice-Chancellor announced the recent establishment of the Centre for Gender Diversity and Social Inclusion to actively mentor female candidates and address the imbalance. Despite severe infrastructural challenges that have affected its competitiveness in student admissions, university officials showcased significant academic achievements. The School of Law recently celebrated a historic milestone, with 27 out of 47 graduates passing their professional entrance examinations on their first attempt. Furthermore, the university’s flagship Practical Training Programme (PTP) continues to drive regional development by deploying students to local communities for advocacy and skills training. The initiative, directed by Professor Stanley K. Dary, was commended by the committee. As UBIDS navigates its complex early years of independence, university management is urgently appealing for targeted government interventions—including special financial dispensation for new universities and integrated infrastructure projects—to stabilise its academic framework and secure the institution’s future.

items.title: Delta reduces inherited debt by N400bn, targets 2027 clearance
items.description: By Egufe Yafugborhi ASABA — The Delta State Government says it has reduced the state’s inherited debt from N463 billion to N63 billion and is targeting full repayment of the outstanding balance by the first quarter of 2027. The Commissioner for Economic Planning, Mr Sonny Ekedayen, disclosed this at the 2026 budget stakeholders’ engagement held in Asaba on Friday. Ekedayen attributed the reported N400 billion reduction to what he described as the Oborevwori administration’s prudent financial management and responsible use of public resources. He said: “We have been able to reduce our legacy debt from N463 billion to N63 billion. We are also working towards clearing the outstanding balance by the first quarter of 2027. “This achievement reflects the commitment of this administration to prudent financial management and responsible utilisation of public resources.” The commissioner said the state government would prioritise roads and other critical infrastructure in the proposed 2027 budget, citing their importance to economic growth and improved access to communities. He said the state’s expenditure structure currently allocated about 70 per cent to capital projects and 30 per cent to recurrent expenditure, adding that the government intended to sustain the emphasis on capital development in the next budget. The Asagba of Asaba, Prof. Epiphany Azinge, called for greater citizens’ participation in the budget preparation process, while commending the state government for its reported budget performance. Azinge said residents and other stakeholders should be given opportunities to contribute to decisions on projects and programmes that directly affect their communities. Meanwhile, civil society organisations at the engagement welcomed plans by the Delta State House of Assembly to introduce legislation regulating housing issues. They said appropriate legislation would help address challenges in the housing sector and provide a framework for improved regulation. items.title: SIAO 2026 : Des vendeurs illicites de tickets d'entrée interpellés, 160 tickets saisis par la Police nationale
items.description: La Police nationale a interpellé plusieurs individus impliqués dans la revente illicite de tickets d'entrée à la 18ᵉ édition du Salon international de l'artisanat de Ouagadougou (SIAO 2026). L'opération, menée sur le site de l'événement, a permis la saisie de 160 tickets d'une valeur nominale de 500 et 1 000 FCFA. Alors que le SIAO 2026 bat son plein à Ouagadougou, certains individus profitent de l'affluence des visiteurs pour se livrer à la revente illicite de tickets d'entrée. Leur mode opératoire consiste à acheter un grand nombre de tickets aux points de vente, avant de les revendre à des prix supérieurs aux tarifs officiels. Grâce à la collaboration des citoyens, les équipes de police judiciaire de la Commission sécurité du SIAO 2026 ont réussi à interpeller des membres de ce réseau. Au total, 160 tickets ont été saisis au cours de l'opération. La Police nationale a salué la vigilance des citoyens, dont les signalements ont contribué à l'interpellation des suspects. Elle a également invité les festivaliers à se procurer leurs tickets exclusivement auprès des points de vente officiels, aux tarifs réglementaires. Elle a, par ailleurs, exhorté les visiteurs à signaler tout comportement suspect aux agents de sécurité présents sur le site et à respecter les consignes de sécurité afin de garantir le bon déroulement de cette 18ᵉ édition du SIAO. items.title: Customs deploys AI tools to tackle fake news, online scams
items.description: By Godwin Oritse The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) has begun deploying artificial intelligence and digital data-tracking tools to combat fake news and online scams capable of damaging its public image. The Comptroller-General of Customs, Adewale Adeniyi, disclosed this at the recently concluded NECCIPR Roundtable 2026 in Lagos. He was represented by the Service’s National Public Relations Officer, Deputy Comptroller Abdullahi Maiwada. Adeniyi said it was important for the Service to ensure that members of the public understood the reasons behind its policies, operations and enforcement activities. Speaking on the theme, “Algorithm Influence and Public Relations,” Maiwada said artificial intelligence had become increasingly important to Customs operations, including risk management and strategic communication. He explained that the technology was being used to assess risks associated with imported goods, classify consignments according to their risk levels and guide appropriate Customs interventions. According to him, AI can also analyse public sentiment and provide insights into how people perceive the activities of the Service. Maiwada said Customs was using available digital platforms to establish facts and working with other relevant agencies to identify and apprehend those responsible for spreading misleading information. He said: “The role of AI cannot be overemphasised, especially within our operations. Over the years, AI has been deployed in our core operational duties as well as strategic communication. “AI has also been deployed to aid risk management, which involves assessment of the risks in imported items so that they can be categorised according to their different levels of risk to enable appropriate Customs interventions.” Earlier, the convener of the NECCIPR Roundtable 2026, Nkechi Ali-Balogun, said the event was founded on the belief that public relations professionals should not only manage messages but also play a leading role in shaping national discourse. She said this year’s theme examined the growing influence of algorithms and artificial intelligence on public opinion and the flow of information. “When machines decide what we see, who is really shaping the Nigerian mind? Who now controls the flow of information that shapes what Nigerians believe? We live in a rapidly changing world, powered by AI, where a single algorithm can shape political narratives, throw out conspiracy theories, and dictate what millions read, believe, and share,” Ali-Balogun said. items.title: Adeboye urges journalists to verify stories before publication
items.description: Says misinformation threatens public trust, clarifies prayer-walk photo, Tinubu comment By OLAYINKA LATONA The General Overseer of the Redeemed Christian Church of God, RCCG, Pastor Enoch Adejare Adeboye, has urged journalists and social media influencers to verify information thoroughly before publishing, warning that misinformation could damage reputations and erode public trust. Adeboye spoke at a monthly special thanksgiving service and prayer session organised for social media influencers, creative industry practitioners, content creators and drama ministers at the church’s national headquarters, Throne of Grace Parish, Ebute-Metta, Lagos. He said media practitioners and content creators had a responsibility to investigate claims before disseminating them, noting that unverified reports could mislead the public. The cleric used the occasion to address two claims about him that had circulated in the media. He denied protesting against former President Goodluck Jonathan, explaining that a widely circulated photograph of him in white and green attire carrying a placard was taken during a prayer walk in 2020. According to him, the walk was organised in compliance with an instruction from the Christian Association of Nigeria, CAN, for churches to hold prayer walks in their neighbourhoods. “It is true I carried a placard. It was a prayer walk. CAN said we should do a prayer walk near our churches. That is what I did in Ebute Meta. A walk is a walk,” he said. Adeboye pointed out that Jonathan left office in 2015, five years before the prayer walk took place during the administration of former President Muhammadu Buhari. “And everybody swallowed it and believed I protested against Jonathan. Nobody checked,” he said. He also faulted reports that, in his comments on President Bola Tinubu, he had said the President had “done his best”. Adeboye recalled speaking in the United States about the abduction of children in Oriire community, Oyo State, and stating that Tinubu, as Commander-in-Chief, had issued the necessary orders for their rescue. He said his remarks were subsequently presented as an endorsement of the President’s handling of the security situation. “Somebody then reported, ‘Pastor Adeboye said the president has done his best,’ and we all swallowed it. When I said the US should not bomb us anymore, that was not news. When I said the US should help us deal with the terrorists, that was not news. God have mercy on journalists,” he said. Recalling his undergraduate days, Adeboye said he took an elective course in the Mass Communication Department, where he was taught the principles of investigative journalism and the need to establish facts before publishing a report. He urged social media influencers to use their platforms responsibly and avoid circulating information that had not been properly verified. In his sermon, Adeboye described potential as a God-given ability bestowed on every human being at birth, stressing that no one was created by mistake. Using the bee and wasp as illustrations, he said different individuals could respond differently to the same opportunities, just as the two insects produce different substances from the same flower. He warned that people’s potential could remain dormant if they failed to develop and deploy it. “There are many journalists who could become world-class but will never go beyond their native towns because their potential was never activated,” he said. Adeboye urged those who had misused or failed to develop their potential to turn to God in repentance, saying divine mercy could help them fulfil their capabilities. The post Adeboye urges journalists to verify stories before publication appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: No more washing up: How Airbnb’s new house rules have divided hosts and guests
items.description: When Lisa Clewes returned to her Welsh holiday let after a group of guests checked out, she was horrified by the mess. Just days earlier, she had met the group in person and helped with their luggage. But after a dinner party, the house was left “in a complete mess” with broken glasses, drinks cans on the floor, pans full of food on the table and fish guts left in the garden. “It was really unbelievable. Had I had another booking the same day, I would have had to cancel or delay check-in,” says Clewes. She charges a cleaning fee that covers around 75% of the cost of a cleaner and asks guests to empty the fridge, put rubbish in the bins and load the dishwasher. But Airbnb’s new rules mean hosts can no longer ask guests to do jobs normally carried out by cleaners, including washing and putting away dishes, stripping beds and taking rubbish off site. The updated guidelines, which apply to bookings made globally from 20 November, state that hosts can now set seven standard house rules and add other “reasonable” requests. Clewes says it typically takes cleaners four hours to turn around her three-bedroom property. She fears guests leaving more mess could mean hiring extra cleaners and increasing costs – expenses that may ultimately be passed on to her guests. The changes have come as a relief to guests like Jessica Newhook, who says she has been faced with lengthy checkout lists, often on top of hefty cleaning fees. She booked an Airbnb in Florida for a family reunion of 11 guests and says they had to “leave the property move-in ready for the cleaners”, despite paying a $250 (£187) cleaning fee. Newhook says the host told them to wash and fold towels, clean the bedding and kitchen, and sweep and mop the floors. She was also warned by the host that their behaviour needed to improve or they could be told to leave, because they had left chairs blocking bins. “We had rules about everything and it was not relaxing at all.” While Newhook likes the home comforts of staying in an Airbnb, she says the combination of relentless rules and rising cleaning fees has taken away much of its appeal. “It is getting to the point where a hotel is cheaper and I know what to expect.” Krissi Foskett, 46, from Glasgow, runs a national cleaning company and regularly stays in Airbnb properties so “can see the issue from both sides”. During a recent stay in Stafford, she paid a £35 cleaning fee but was still asked to strip the beds, put on a wash, empty bins and carry rubbish down a long track to a recycling area. “I don’t particularly mind doing those things, but it did make me question what exactly I was paying the additional cleaning fee for,” she says. For Foskett, there is a difference between being a considerate guest – “putting your dirty dishes in the dishwasher” – and being “expected to prepare the property for the next guests”. Through her cleaning business, she has also seen the other extreme, with teams arriving to find broken furniture, vomit and pet urine. While she sympathises with hosts facing tight turnarounds and rising cleaning costs, these should not be passed on to guests, she says. “If you’re running an Airbnb as a business, professional cleaning is a cost of doing business.” Anthony Marsh, who co-owns a cabin retreat in North Yorkshire with his husband, used to list five of their 12 properties on Airbnb, but says the new rules have prompted him to reduce this number to just two. His concern with the changes is that “Airbnb has effectively given guests permission to come and leave properties a tip, and a host can’t do anything about it”. He believes asking guests to wash their pots and put out the bins is hardly unreasonable and, with a small cleaning team and tight turnaround times, he worries extra mess could leave properties unready for the next arrivals. “It’s common sense and common decency,” he says. His company does not charge a cleaning fee, and Marsh says most guests are respectful. But fees are more common than not. Some 63.2% of Airbnb listings charge a cleaning fee, with an average cost of £55 according to data from AirROI. Laura Lewis runs a directory that helps holiday-let owners market their properties and connect with potential guests. Many of her clients also list on Airbnb and she says most are unhappy with the new rules, arguing that asking guests to wash up is a matter of basic respect. “Some people say it’s factored into the cleaning fee, but I wouldn’t leave a holiday let with all the washing-up to do. It’s not the right thing,” she says. The announcement has added to growing frustration among owners following increases in Airbnb’s commission rates last year. Many are investing in their own websites and social media to attract direct bookings and avoid platform fees. Lewis has taken the same approach with the three treehouses on her farm – most of her bookings are already direct and she now plans to remove her listings from Airbnb altogether. Not all hosts are concerned about the changes, however. Matt Prosz, who hosts and manages other Airbnb properties full-time, believes the update will improve the guest experience without changing how most people behave. Guests at his property in south-west London are asked only to lock up and return the keys. “People sometimes strip the beds or do things without me asking, and that’s nice for my cleaners, but I don’t expect it.” Prosz doubts the changes will lead to guests leaving properties in a worse state, pointing to Airbnb’s mutual review system. “If I put a big chore list, I wouldn’t expect a five-star review and vice versa – if a guest leaves the place in a state, you’re not going to give them a good review.” He believes the system encourages both sides to behave reasonably, and that most guests will continue to treat properties with respect. “Airbnb is trying to cut out the silly stuff because it’s not a good guest experience.”

items.title: Millions of women, young girls denied jobs, education as ITUC-Afraid demands urgent action
items.description: By Victor Ahiuma-Young The African Regional Organisation of the International Trade Union Confederation, ITUC-Africa, has raised the alarm over the growing care crisis across the continent, warning that millions of women and young girls are being denied employment, education and economic opportunities because of the disproportionate burden of unpaid care work placed on them. The organisation called on African governments, the African Union (AU) and Regional Economic Communities (RECs) to urgently invest in sustainable care systems, improve working conditions for care workers and introduce policies that recognise, reduce and redistribute unpaid care responsibilities. In a statement issued to commemorate the International Day for Care and Support, ITUC-Africa General Secretary, Akhator Joel Odigie, said care work remained undervalued, underpaid and largely ignored in public policies and national budgets, despite its enormous contribution to the survival of economies and societies. Marking the international day under the theme, “Building Sustainable Care and Support Systems Through Decent Work,” the organisation stressed that care work was indispensable to economic development and social wellbeing but continued to receive inadequate recognition and investment. “Care sustains every economy and society. Yet paid and unpaid care work remains undervalued, underpaid and largely overlooked in public policy and national budgets, despite its vital social and economic contribution,” the statement declared. ITUC-Africa expressed particular concern over the disproportionate burden borne by African women and girls, noting that women across the continent spend more than three times as many hours as men performing unpaid care work. According to the organisation, the situation has become a major obstacle to women’s economic empowerment and participation in the labour market. “More than one-third of African women outside the labour force are excluded from employment because of care responsibilities, compared with fewer than one in twenty men,” the statement disclosed. It further warned that young women were particularly disadvantaged, especially in rural communities, where unpaid domestic and care responsibilities significantly restrict their access to education, vocational training and decent employment. “In rural West Africa, they spend four times as many hours on unpaid care work as young men, limiting their opportunities to pursue education, access vocational training, secure decent jobs, and participate in trade unions,” ITUC-Africa stated. The organisation said the situation was perpetuating gender inequality and reinforcing the economic exclusion of women, particularly those from poor and vulnerable households. It also drew attention to the difficult conditions confronting millions of workers in the care economy, including domestic workers, community health workers, early childhood educators, nurses and home-based carers. Many of these workers, most of whom are women and a significant number of whom are migrants, reportedly operate in the informal economy, earning poverty wages and working without adequate social protection. They are also exposed to violence, harassment and other forms of workplace exploitation. “Domestic workers, community health workers, early childhood educators, nurses and home-based carers, most of them women and many of them migrants, too often work informally, for poverty wages, without social protection, and exposed to violence and harassment,” the statement said. In a particularly strong warning, ITUC-Africa argued that the poor treatment of care workers ultimately undermined the quality of services available to society. “Poor working conditions for care workers mean poor quality care for everyone,” it emphasised. The organisation further observed that Africa had the weakest care coverage in the world, even as demand for care services continued to rise due to population growth, urbanisation, the climate crisis and an increasingly ageing population. Against this background, ITUC-Africa called for urgent government intervention to establish accessible, affordable and quality public care systems capable of addressing the growing needs of African societies. It urged governments to invest in childcare, long-term care and health services, as well as essential infrastructure such as water, electricity and clean cooking facilities to reduce the amount of unpaid labour performed by women and girls. The organisation also called for the implementation of the 5R framework for decent care work, alongside the 2024 International Labour Organisation (ILO) Resolution on Decent Work and the Care Economy, through comprehensive national care policies. On labour rights and legal protection, ITUC-Africa urged African governments to ratify and implement key ILO conventions, including Convention No. 189 on Domestic Workers, Convention No. 156 on Workers with Family Responsibilities, Convention No. 183 on Maternity Protection, Convention No. 190 on Violence and Harassment, and Convention No. 102 on Social Security. It maintained that the protection of care workers must go beyond policy declarations to guarantee decent wages, formal employment arrangements, safe working environments and comprehensive social protection. “Guarantee decent work for all care workers: living wages, equal pay for work of equal value, formal contracts, safe workplaces, social protection, and the rights to organise and bargain collectively,” the organisation demanded. ITUC-Africa also called for the extension of social protection to informal economy workers and unpaid carers, while urging governments to provide adequately funded paid parental leave for both women and men. According to the organisation, addressing the care crisis requires a fundamental shift in how African societies distribute care responsibilities, finance care services and recognise the contributions of those who provide essential care. It argued that care responsibilities should not continue to fall disproportionately on women, particularly when such arrangements prevent them from securing decent employment, advancing their education and participating fully in public and economic life. Reaffirming the labour movement’s commitment to addressing the challenges, ITUC-Africa pledged to intensify efforts to organise care workers, particularly young women and workers in the informal economy, to strengthen their collective voice and improve their working conditions. “ITUC-Africa commits to organising care workers, especially young women and workers in the informal economy, to give them a stronger collective voice, and to keep care at the heart of our struggle for social justice on the continent,” the statement said. The statement added with a renewed call for African governments and regional institutions to place care work at the centre of their development priorities. The organisation maintained that building sustainable care and support systems through decent work was not merely a labour rights issue but a critical requirement for achieving gender equality, economic inclusion and social justice across Africa. The post Millions of women, young girls denied jobs, education as ITUC-Afraid demands urgent action appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: La vida truncada de Fran, el teleoperador cordobés: “Era pura dulzura”
items.description: Sus compañeros de trabajo le regañaron por renunciar a un empleo con más sueldo y mejores condiciones. Francisco José Barbero Liébanas, uno de los 69 fallecidos en el accidente ferroviario de Urda, trabajaba desde hacía un año como teleoperador en una entidad financiera , pero su sueño era poder trabajar “de lo suyo”, de profesor de Lengua y Literatura. Por fin le había salido una oportunidad en una academia. “Fran, no seas burro, piensa en ti primero”, le dijo su colega Ángeles Millán. “Preséntate al menos”, le insistió. Barbero, de 32 años, se resistía. Tenía un segundo trabajo: cuidaba a una anciana a cambio de una habitación en Madrid y tenía sus dudas. “No puedo dejar a la señora sola”, contestó. Eso, dice Millán, te da una idea de cómo era de generoso. Seguir leyendo

items.title: La actuación de tres policías que iban en los trenes siniestrados salvó vidas
items.description: José Luis Moris es un policía nacional sevillano que trabaja cubriendo la noche en Puente de Vallecas (Madrid). El pasado miércoles, como tantas otras veces, salió de su turno nocturno y cogió el tren para regresar a Sevilla y reunirse con su mujer y su hija recién nacida, de pocos meses. Era un trayecto que hacía semanalmente para reencontrarse con su familia. En esta ocasión cogió el Iryo que salía a las 7.54 hacía la capital hispalense. Ataviado con su material de trabajo habitual, que lleva siempre por si acaso, y que incluía un botiquín repartido en los bolsillos de un chaleco, se sentó en su asiento. Tan solo 59 minutos más tarde, noqueado por el tremendo golpe que sufrió su convoy, parado a la altura de la estación de Urda (Toledo), al ser embestido por detrás por un AVE, se encontraría inmerso en un escenario de guerra apagando fuegos y haciendo torniquetes. Su labor, como la de otras dos agentes de la UFAM (la Unidad de Atención a la Familia y a la Mujer de la Policía Nacional) que también iban en el tren camino de un congreso, resultó providencial en los primeros momentos del brutal siniestro. items.title: Pologne : Tusk accuse le président et son prédécesseur de «détruire l’État de droit» sur fond de crise constitutionnelle
items.description: Le Premier ministre polonais Donald Tusk a accuse, le 31 octobre, le president Karol Nawrocki, son predecesseur Andrzej Duda et le parti d'opposition Droit et justice (PiS) de « detruire l'etat de droit » en Pologne. Ces accusations interviennent en pleine crise autour du Tribunal constitutionnel, dont la direction fait l'objet d'un affrontement entre le gouvernement et la presidence. Dans une allocution a la nation, Tusk a denonce « une nouvelle etape du processus de destruction de l'etat de droit », qu'il impute au PiS et aux deux presidents. Il a exclu tout compromis, affirmant que l'opposition avait rejete les solutions proposees par la majorite pour resoudre le conflit. Il a egalement estime qu'aucun responsable politique, pas meme le president, ne pouvait imposer ses decisions a un tribunal ni intimider ses juges. Une bataille pour la direction du Tribunal constitutionnel Au cœur de la crise se trouve le Tribunal constitutionnel, charge de verifier la conformite des lois a la Constitution. Les tensions se sont notamment aggravees apres l'election de Maciej Berek, ancien membre du gouvernement Tusk, comme juge constitutionnel. Nawrocki a refuse de recevoir son serment, bloquant son entree en fonctions. Le 30 octobre, le ministre de la Justice Waldemar Zurek a demande la suspension du president du Tribunal, Bogdan Swieczkowski, ainsi que la levee de son immunite. Parallelement, la juge Anna Korwin-Piotrowska a revendique la direction provisoire de l'institution et annonce la suspension de Swieczkowski et de son adjoint, Bartlomiej Sochanski. Tous deux contestent leur mise a l'ecart et affirment rester en fonctions. Ces mesures ont provoque de nouvelles tensions devant le Tribunal, a Varsovie. Des manifestants se sont rassembles aux abords du bâtiment, place sous surveillance policiere. Plusieurs personnes ont tente de franchir les barrieres de securite et ont ete interpellees. Face a cette situation, Nawrocki a interrompu son voyage vers le Senegal pour rentrer d'urgence a Varsovie. L'opposition denonce une tentative de coup d'etat De retour dans la capitale, le president polonais a denonce un coup de force contre le Tribunal constitutionnel. Le PiS, dirige par Jaroslaw Kaczynski, a egalement accuse le gouvernement de chercher a prendre le controle de l'institution, allant jusqu'a qualifier les evenements de tentative de coup d'etat. Tusk a, de son cote, defendu l'intervention de la police, presentant les mesures de son gouvernement comme necessaires au retablissement de l'independance de la justice. La crise a egalement suscite des reactions a l'etranger. Le 1er novembre, Viktor Orban a apporte son soutien a Nawrocki, accusant Tusk d'avoir tente d'organiser un coup d'etat contre son propre peuple. Ce nouvel affrontement prolonge un conflit institutionnel ouvert en 2015, lorsque les nominations controversees de juges sous le gouvernement PiS avaient declenche une crise durable autour du Tribunal constitutionnel. Depuis son retour au pouvoir en 2023, Tusk affirme vouloir retablir l'etat de droit, mais ses methodes sont contestees par le president et l'opposition. Les deux camps revendiquent desormais la defense de l'ordre constitutionnel polonais.

items.title: Bayern Munich : Ismaël Saibari opéré de la cheville après sa blessure face à Dortmund
items.description: L’international marocain Ismaël Saibari, attaquant du Bayern Munich, a subi une intervention chirurgicale à la cheville après la blessure contractée lors du match nul (2-2) de son équipe face au Borussia Dortmund, samedi, dans le cadre du championnat allemand. De leur côté, les examens médicaux ont révélé une blessure aux ischio-jambiers chez Serge Gnabry. Le Bayern Munich, champion en titre de Bundesliga, a publié dimanche un communiqué faisant le point sur l’état de santé de ses joueurs, après que plusieurs autres éléments de l’effectif ont rejoint l’infirmerie, aux côtés de Manuel Neuer, Jamal Musiala et Luis Díaz, qui souffrent déjà de problèmes physiques. Sans préciser la durée d’indisponibilité des deux joueurs, le club bavarois a indiqué : « Saibari souffre d’une rupture du ligament tibio-fibulaire antérieur de la cheville droite et a déjà subi une intervention chirurgicale. Quant à Gnabry, il souffre d’une blessure musculaire aux ischio-jambiers de la cuisse gauche. » Le communiqué ne fait aucune mention de Michael Olise, qui a quitté le terrain en boitant dans les dernières minutes de la rencontre face à Dortmund. Le Bayern a également précisé que l’opération subie par Saibari, le joueur marocain recruté dans le cadre d’un transfert important lors du dernier mercato estival, s’était déroulée avec succès. Âgé de 31 ans, Serge Gnabry venait tout juste de retrouver sa condition physique après avoir manqué la participation de l’équipe nationale allemande à la Coupe du monde en raison d’une blessure aux adducteurs. Cette succession de blessures pèse lourdement sur l’effectif bavarois et accentue la pression sur les joueurs disponibles, alors que l’entraîneur Vincent Kompany a déjà manqué trois rencontres pour cause de maladie. Le Bayern a même été contraint d’aligner trois joueurs évoluant au poste d’arrière gauche au cours de la seconde période du match contre Dortmund, illustrant l’ampleur des absences au sein de l’équipe. Le club bavarois, qui avait déjà indiqué ne pas envisager de recruter lors du prochain mercato hivernal de janvier, se déplacera mardi prochain sur la pelouse de l’Atlético de Madrid dans le cadre de la Ligue des champions. The post Bayern Munich : Ismaël Saibari opéré de la cheville après sa blessure face à Dortmund appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Opep+ : les pays producteurs devraient maintenir leurs objectifs de production en décembre
items.description: Les sept principaux membres de l'Opep+ devraient maintenir leurs objectifs de production de petrole inchanges pour decembre, lors d'une reunion prevue ce 1er novembre, ont indique le 31 octobre trois sources proches des discussions a Reuters. La reunion en ligne, prevue a 12h (GMT), doit reunir l'Arabie saoudite, la Russie, l'Irak, le Koweït, l'Algerie, le Kazakhstan et Oman. Cette decision serait conforme aux attentes du marche, alors que le groupe ne devrait proceder a de nouveaux ajustements qu'a partir de l'annee prochaine. Les pays du Golfe cherchent a augmenter leurs exportations, perturbees depuis plusieurs mois par la guerre entre les etats-Unis et l'Iran. Malgre les relevements successifs des objectifs de production, plusieurs membres continuent toutefois de produire en dessous des niveaux fixes. L'Opep+, qui rassemble l'Organisation des pays exportateurs de petrole (Opep) et ses partenaires, dont la Russie, a progressivement releve ses objectifs de production au cours de 2026. En septembre, elle a acheve la levee progressive d'une reduction de l'offre de 1,65 million de barils par jour, decidee en 2023. Les objectifs avaient deja ete maintenus sans changement pour octobre et novembre. Le groupe conserve neanmoins un autre niveau de reductions de production, d'environ 2 millions de barils par jour, qui concerne la majorite de ses membres et doit rester en vigueur jusqu'a la fin de 2026. Des quotas pour 2027 en preparation Avant de fixer les nouveaux quotas pour 2027, l'Opep+ doit achever, au cours du quatrieme trimestre, une evaluation des capacites de production de ses membres. Cette revision doit permettre de determiner les niveaux de reference qui serviront a etablir les futures quotas et a orienter la levee progressive des reductions encore en vigueur. Selon des sources citees precedemment par Reuters, le groupe devrait ainsi privilegier la preparation de sa politique de production pour 2027 plutot que de modifier ses objectifs au cours du dernier trimestre de cette annee.

items.title: Upper Dir police claim arresting 5 suspects over alleged assault of minor boy
items.description: LOWER DIR: Police in Upper Dir said on Sunday they have arrested five of the six suspects over the alleged assault and intimidation of a teenage boy, a purported video of which was circulated on social media. Wari Circle Deputy Superintendent of Police (DSP) Fakhr-i-Alam confirmed the arrests to Dawn . The incident took place on Oct 25, according to a first information report (FIR), dated Oct 30 and seen by Dawn , filed by Wari police on the boy’s complaint. The case invoked Sections 364-A (kidnapping or abducting an underage person), 342 (punishment for wrongful confinement), 506 (criminal intimidation), 147 (rioting) and 149 (unlawful assembly) of the Pakistan Penal Code . In the FIR, the boy alleged that on the day of the incident, a friend of his called him to a place where two men, including an unidentified tehsildar, forcibly made him board a car and took him to an under-construction house in Shinkarai. There, he was allegedly assaulted and threatened by the two men who demanded an “unnatural” act. The FIR nominated a total of six people, including his friend. Those arrested excluded one of the two men who made the boy board the car. The boy alleged that the two men who forced him into the car and three others present at the house kept him confined in a room for around three hours. The complainant further alleged that the two men who brought him there and another person recorded the incident on their mobile phones, while two others delivered blows to him with kicks, punches, and sticks. “Due to their blows, I sustained severe pain in my right shin, right and left arms, and across the rest of my body,” the boy said in the FIR. The complainant further claimed that the incident stemmed from WhatsApp conversations among friends. According to the complainant, the delay in reporting the incident was due to death threats from the suspects, who had also threatened to share the video. The video, reportedly recorded by some of the suspects, surfaced on social media days after the alleged incident, prompting police to take action. The allegations levelled in the FIR have yet to be independently verified by Dawn . Police said they had initiated an investigation into the case. Child protection NGO Sahil estimates that at least 558 cases of child abductions were reported across the country in the first six months of 2026. Earlier this month, police in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Charsadda arrested a man for allegedly assaulting a five-year-old boy. In late August, Mansehra police held two men after a mother alleged they assaulted her nine-year-old son.

items.title: Police arrest three over suspected ICPC ID forgery in Nasarawa
items.description: By Edwin Philip, Lafia The Nasarawa State Police Command has arrested three persons over the alleged forgery of an identity card bearing the name of the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) and recovered an unregistered vehicle suspected to have been stolen. The suspects were identified as Mohammed Umar, Mohammed Nuhu and Ibrahim Suleiman. They were arrested by operatives of the Anti-Kidnapping Unit during a routine patrol around Bukan Sidi, Lafia. The Police Public Relations Officer, Ramhan Nansel, disclosed this in a statement issued to journalists on Sunday in Lafia. According to the statement, the operatives intercepted a Lexus IS 250 without a registration number while the three suspects were travelling in it. During questioning, Nuhu allegedly introduced himself as an ICPC officer and presented an identification card purportedly issued by the commission. However, when Umar, who was driving the vehicle, was asked to explain its ownership, he reportedly failed to provide a satisfactory account, prompting the arrest of all three occupants for further investigation. The police said preliminary findings indicated that the ICPC identification card presented by Nuhu was allegedly forged. Nuhu reportedly told investigators that he accompanied the driver from Kaduna State to Lafia because Umar did not have a valid driver’s licence. The statement further disclosed that investigations were ongoing into an allegation linking Suleiman to a group identified as the Eiye Confraternity. The police said the allegations were being investigated to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident and determine the level of involvement of each suspect. The suspects remain in police custody as investigations continue. The command said they would be charged to court upon conclusion of the investigation. It added that efforts were being intensified to establish the vehicle’s ownership and determine whether other offences were connected to the incident. The Commissioner of Police, Nasarawa State Command, Shetima Jauro Mohamed, reiterated the command’s commitment to proactive policing, intelligence-led operations and sustained efforts to combat crime across the state. The post Police arrest three over suspected ICPC ID forgery in Nasarawa appeared first on Vanguard News .
