items.title: ¿Qué causó el accidente? La secuencia paso a paso de una cadena de fallos que el sistema no detuvo
items.description: En el accidente ferroviario de Urda han muerto al menos 69 personas y hay más de 200 heridos, según la primera nota de la AITAT, la autoridad independiente que investiga los accidentes de transporte. El final es un choque violento: un AVE de Renfe alcanzó por detrás a un Iryo que estaba detenido. Pero, ¿qué había pasado antes? Seguir leyendo Metodología Los modelos de los trenes han sido construidos a partir de imágenes usando herramientas de inteligencia artificial. Las posiciones y velocidades del AVE son estimaciones a partir de los datos públicos de geolocalización de Renfe, que llegan con unos 40-60 segundos de retraso; para el cálculo se han utilizado dos agentes IA. Iryo no publica posiciones: la de su tren procede del relato de la maquinista, del ministerio y de la AITAT. La posición de las señales (semáforo) salen de los esquemas de vía de Adif, y las citas, de los audios publicados y de las dos comparecencias del ministro de Transporte. Para la reconstrucción inicial, se han usado imágenes públicas del AVE y del Iryo. Para los mapas, se usan IGN / PNOA MDT05 (relieve local), Copernicus DEM (DLR/Airbus) vía OpenTopography (perfil de respaldo y relieve alternativo), OpenStreetMap.

items.title: Las vidas truncadas en el tren: “Gracias por quererme, por entenderme, por ser el mejor padre del mundo”
items.description: La mañana del miércoles España despertó con un soleado día de otoño que, en cuestión de minutos, quedaría ensombrecido por una gigantesca tragedia. Poco después del amanecer, 147 personas se apresuraban en la estación madrileña de Atocha para coger un tren Iryo que salía a las 7.54 horas hacia Sevilla. La joven atleta Julieta Gallego, que había llegado desde Berlín para disfrutar de unos días de vacaciones en Córdoba con sus abuelos; la podóloga argentina de 32 años, Ana María Conte, que regresaba a su lugar de residencia junto a su hermano Zacarías; el revisor portugués de 49 años Nelson Bernardino, que atendía con su uniforme a los pasajeros; o la exministra Fátima Báñez, de 59 años y actual presidenta de la Fundación CEOE, que acudía a los actos por el Día de la Empresa en Andalucía. Seguir leyendo

items.title: El maquinista de Angrois al operador de Atocha: “Que se aísle de la tele y la prensa: le pueden hacer mucho daño”
items.description: Francisco José Garzón (Monforte de Lemos, 65 años) responde al teléfono al quinto tono. No es fácil hablar con él, tampoco cuando descuelga. Hay ruido de fondo, su voz suena tranquila pero evasiva. “Yo te pido, por favor, que hables antes con mi abogado. Todo lo que diga tiene que contar con su permiso”, dice al periodista. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Lecciones alemanas del peor accidente de la alta velocidad de la historia
items.description: El 3 de junio de 1998 quedó marcado en negro en la historia de Alemania. Un tren de alta velocidad descarriló a 200 kilómetros por hora en el término municipal de Eschede, en el Estado de Baja Sajonia. El convoy impactó contra un puente de carretera y la infraestructura se derrumbó sobre varios vagones. Fallecieron 101 personas y 108 resultaron heridas. Es el peor accidente de la alta velocidad en el mundo. La seguridad es desde entonces la prioridad en la red ferroviaria alemana, también a costa de reducir velocidad y la comodidad de los usuarios. Seguir leyendo

items.title: El tercer tren de Urda: la espera bajo un puente a dos kilómetros de la tragedia
items.description: El semáforo sigue en rojo. A dos metros por debajo de un puente quedó detenido un AVE lleno de pasajeros que aún no sabían que, a dos kilómetros, acababa de ocurrir una tragedia que ha dejado por ahora 69 muertos . Este sábado, cuatro días después del accidente, una vecina señala desde arriba dónde estaba la cabecera, por dónde bajaron los viajeros y el camino que tomaron quienes salieron a ayudar. Al fondo siguen los vagones destrozados del Renfe y el Iryo y las grúas. Ramón Rubio de Castro viajaba en aquel tercer tren. “Cuando uno está a pocos metros de una tragedia así, entiende de verdad lo cerca que puede estar todo de haber sido completamente diferente”, dice por teléfono. Este sábado por la mañana, desde la carretera, este periódico pudo ver un tren de Renfe que era trasladado hacia Madrid por la línea que permanece cerrada al tráfico ferroviario desde el accidente . Seguir leyendo

items.title: Puente intenta bajar la presión con un gran plan de refuerzo de la seguridad del AVE
items.description: Óscar Puente no ha pasado el fin de semana como un político al borde de la dimisión. Más bien al contrario. Apuntalado por su líder, Pedro Sánchez, que le ha pedido que siga y que le ofrezca soluciones, Puente lleva desde el viernes en una especie de reunión permanente con sus colaboradores y técnicos de todo tipo para plantear este martes, en el Consejo de Ministros, un plan de acción completo para reforzar la seguridad en la alta velocidad y recuperar esa “confianza quebrada” de la que hablaba el propio Sánchez el viernes. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Puente, de la euforia al desastre en tres días
items.description: El ministro del Club de la Lucha está contra las cuerdas, pero se niega a arrojar la toalla. Óscar Puente (Valladolid, 57 años), al igual que la película noventera de David Fincher con la que se identifica por su desacomplejada pelea diaria con la derecha y los socialistas críticos con Pedro Sánchez, sigue sin dejar a nadie indiferente. Y menos ahora, en su noche más oscura por los 69 fallecidos en Urda (Toledo), la segunda tragedia de la alta velocidad en nueve meses tras la de Adamuz (Córdoba), con 46 muertos: no solo la derecha sino el Frente Amplio y Comisiones Obreras piden su cese o dimisión. Mientras, el PSOE guarda silencio dividido sobre la idoneidad de la continuidad de su enfant terrible a menos de un mes de las elecciones generales. “Mis causas son mas importantes que mi vida. No tomo decisiones pensando en mí, sino en si son útiles. Y el que manda ha considerado que soy útil”, compartió Puente el viernes en un corrillo informal con periodistas tras “dar la cara” en una rueda de prensa de dos horas sin límite de preguntas ni medios vetados. Se mostró entero. Solo incómodo en una de las ocasiones, cuando se le espetó por enésima vez que debía marcharse y sin honor alguno. El martes le espera otra sesión que puede precipitar su futuro, en la Diputación Permanente del Congreso. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Feijóo gira la campaña hacia el perfil gestor del PP
items.description: La escenografía de este viernes en el PP no dejaba lugar a dudas. Alberto Núñez Feijóo reunió en la sede del PP a una quincena de expertos en la red ferroviaria de dentro y fuera del partido para estudiar las causas del devastador accidente de Urda. A su espalda, en la pantalla a toda pared de la segunda planta de Génova, se leía en grandes letras: “Gestión. Rigor. Experiencia”. Esas tres palabras definen el mensaje hacia el que el PP reenfoca ahora su estrategia de precampaña, que ha saltado por los aires, como la de todos los partidos, por el cisne negro de Urda. Los populares, que suspendieron los actos electorales por la catástrofe, estudian ahora cómo retomarlos, pero con la idea de proyectar su perfil gestor, que sirve además para tratar de conjurar el riesgo de otro repunte de Vox por una reacción emocional de la sociedad española ante el desastre ferroviario. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Nosotros, los votantes
items.description: ¿Cómo nos sacudiremos esta época? Es como un atuendo grotesco, de un neobarroquismo que hiere la vista, que atufa también, como uno de esos modelos de las galas del Met en las que se valora el desequilibrio y el feísmo, la incomodidad, el precio desorbitado, como el sujetador de 50 millones de Kylie Jenner , síntoma de estos tiempos rendidos a un despilfarro desacomplejado. ¿Cómo nos desharemos de esta época de impudor y grosería? El miércoles, la misma mañana fatal, cuando aún solo se había pronunciado la palabra accidente, un grupo de periodistas comentábamos la pendiente por la que se iba deslizando la campaña electoral. Era previo a la conciencia de la gravedad, de tal forma que todavía se dibujaba una sonrisa casi de resignación en los rostros ante ese azote diario de acusaciones brutales, lenguaje soez y discursos de líderes que, desconocedores de su propio programa, solo saben salir del paso escupiendo exabruptos. Es lo que espera su votante, decía alguien: la sangre. Eso era antes de saber el alcance del choque. También comentábamos esa satisfacción forzada, un tanto irracional, de quien habiendo superado sin superar tantas crisis trata de volver a la casilla de salida con bailes que al parecer levantan el ánimo de los votantes más desanimados. Es lo que espera su votante, decía alguien: recuperar la alegría. Los demás asentíamos sin convencimiento. Como era de esperar, no se dejó atrás el festival del humor que andaban ofreciendo las cadenas, incluida la estatal, para demostrar que las y los políticos también lloran, ríen y follan, por usar el único verbo en alza para contarnos el sexo. Es lo que puede funcionar, añadió alguien, con un votante joven que, desentendido de la división de la izquierda, despierte de su modorra oyendo en Instagram las palabras coño, polla y culo. Si votaran los niños, ay, habría que añadir unas consideraciones sobre los pedos. Hay coordinadoras de intimidad en el cine, pero se ve que aún no han llegado a la televisión. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Mis amigos muertos
items.description: A estas alturas de la vida uno ya tiene en el otro mundo a la mayoría de los que fueron sus mejores amigos. A veces en estas tardes desoladas de otoño pronuncio sus nombres, uno a uno, mientras una melodía de jazz me trasporta a aquellos días felices que compartimos juntos. Imagino que ellos también la están oyendo y si aquí en el mundo de los vivos la tarde es lluviosa pienso que allí en el otro lado también estará lloviendo y algunos de mis amigos habrán ido a algún garito a jugar al póquer. Si la tarde es soleada puede que otros prefieran pasear por el bosque hasta que caiga la niebla. No importa que hayan muerto. Me divierte imaginarlos haciendo lo mismo que hacían en este lado. Algunos seguirán navegando a Ibiza en verano, otros soñarán con rodar nuevas películas, o celebrarán el éxito de su última novela, otros alargarán las sobremesas a la sombra de los pinos hablando de amores perdidos, de viajes, de bellos recuerdos del pasado. En el otro lado estas tardes de otoño olerán a leña de encina en las chimeneas de las casas habitadas por mis amigos muertos. Tal vez ellos quieran saber qué sucede aquí en la tierra. Habrá que decirles que una tragedia humana acaba de romper toda nuestra modernidad en pedazos. ¿Recordáis aquel antiguo glamur de viajar en el tren de alta velocidad? Otra vez ese sueño se ha convertido en un amasijo de hierros lleno de cadáveres. A esta tragedia hay que añadir la locura de unos adolescentes deslumbrados por la violencia que incendian las calles, rompen escaparates y saquean las tiendas de lujo, una orgía que aprovechan los políticos de uno y otro bando. En contrapartida, más allá del dolor por todos los muertos, he levantado el brazo hasta una rama del membrillero y he arrancado suavemente unos membrillos maduros y con la yema de los dedos he frotado su pelusilla que escondía debajo un color de miel, los he colocado en un frutero y he sentido que con este acto, por mi parte, el orden del mundo había sido restablecido.

items.title: Mägo de Oz, muy grandes, muy conflictivos: demandas, disputas por el poder y una película que reabre las heridas del grupo heavy
items.description: Mägo de Oz es la banda más grande del heavy metal español. También la más conflictiva. Algunos pensarán: ¿y Barón Rojo, qué? Otros: ¿y Obús? Pero los números avalan a Mägo de Oz: los miles de asistentes a sus conciertos en España y Latinoamérica durante tres décadas son imbatibles. También en ventas de discos supera a cualquier otro grupo del género duro. Este año, por ejemplo, su nuevo álbum, Malicia: la noche de las brujas (2025), compite en los Grammy Latinos como mejor disco de rock. El juicio resulta menos concluyente cuando se atiende a la calidad musical y al peso histórico del repertorio. Incluso los propios integrantes de Mägo de Oz reconocerían, acaso en privado, el impacto y la trascendencia de las canciones de Barón Rojo, claramente superior al suyo. Seguir leyendo

items.title: La banca cobra hasta 276 euros al año al cliente poco vinculado (y despistado)
items.description: Tener abierta una cuenta en el banco que apenas se usa puede salir muy caro. La banca española llega a cobrar hasta 276 euros al año por el mantenimiento de una cuenta corriente y una tarjeta de débito a los clientes menos vinculados. Es el precio más elevado de entre las once entidades analizadas para el supuesto de un cliente que no cumple con ninguna de las condiciones que exigen las entidades para librarse de las comisiones que figuran en la letra del contrato al abrir una cuenta. Seguir leyendo

items.title: La oposición israelí se atasca tras su victoria electoral
items.description: Acabadas las elecciones en Israel, los ingredientes están claros, pero queda lo más difícil: ligar la salsa. Los resultados definitivos de los comicios, difundidos el viernes, apenas varían el dibujo que se venía esbozando: el Likud, el partido del primer ministro Benjamín Netanyahu, cae de 32 a 27 escaños, pero sigue como primera fuerza. Su coalición, sin embargo, pierde la mayoría parlamentaria, al quedarse en solo 53 escaños de los 120 que tiene la Kneset. En otro país, la conclusión sería que ha ganado la oposición . Pero los 67 escaños restantes se dividen entre 48 para los cuatro partidos judíos —que van desde, sobre todo, la derecha hasta la izquierda secular—y en 19 para las dos listas que representan a los palestinos con pasaporte israelí: un 20% de la población estigmatizada y tratada como ciudadanos de segunda. Y si algo han mostrado los primeros días de contactos es justamente cuánto costará en el Israel de 2026 que los partidos judíos integren a los árabes. Tanto que se habla más ya de nuevas elecciones que de nuevo Gobierno. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Manual de demolición: cómo los estudiantes de Serbia derrotaron a Vucic sin violencia
items.description: Aleksandar Bulajic, estudiante de psicología, de 25 años, camina por el cuartel de operaciones electorales de la Lista Estudiantil, un edificio moderno de oficinas acristaladas, en el barrio de Nuevo Belgrado. Muestra una sala ahora sin gente, solo con ordenadores. Desde ahí, 50 estudiantes recopilaron el domingo 25 de octubre los resultados de las elecciones legislativas de Serbia en 500 colegios electorales , con los que obtuvieron una muestra muy fiable de lo que ocurría en los 8.000 centros del país. Seguir leyendo

items.title: La misión de la ONU en el Sáhara queda en el limbo mientras se dispara el riesgo de escalada bélica
items.description: Vista como paradigma de la impotencia de la comunidad internacional ante un conflicto olvidado, la Misión de Naciones Unidas para el Referéndum del Sáhara Occidental (Minurso) agonizaba este sábado al término de su último mandato anual sin haber cumplido el encargo de organizar la consulta de autodeterminación para la que fue creada en 1991. En un desenlace fuera del guion rutinario de la ONU, con vetos cruzados entre Rusia y EE UU como en el cénit de la Guerra Fría, recibió la sentencia de muerte la noche del viernes dictada por el Consejo de Seguridad, pese a los 11 votos a favor y tres abstenciones obtenidos por la resolución impulsada por Washington. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Estados Unidos somete a referéndum el final del trumpismo
items.description: Con los previstos para este fin de semana, desconvocados y vueltos a convocar para no dar signos de debilidad, Donald Trump habrá dado 28 mítines en la campaña de las legislativas de mitad de mandato, que se celebran el próximo martes en Estados Unidos. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Las ‘midterm’, en mapas y gráficos: qué se vota este martes y cómo llega Trump
items.description: Este martes 3 de noviembre se celebran las elecciones de medio mandato ( midterms ) que decidirán si los republicanos de Donald Trump conservan un Congreso afín o si los demócratas se hacen con el control de una o dos de las Cámaras, lo que permitiría hacer una oposición más agresiva frenando leyes, presupuestos y nombramientos durante los dos años que quedan de su mandato. Según las encuestas, solo el 37% de la población aprueba al actual presidente republicano Donald Trump, y las encuestas muestran que los demócratas están encaminados a lograr la mayoría en el Congreso y el Senado. No es un dato sorprendente, ya que las midterms suelen castigar al partido del presidente. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Glosario ilustrado de las ‘midterms’: conceptos clave para entender las elecciones en EE UU
items.description: Las elecciones legislativas de medio mandato definirán el resto de la presidencia de Trump. Este es el abecé imprescindible para entender lo que hay en juego

items.title: Niños que necesitan a sus padres para dormir: dos especialistas explican qué hay detrás y cómo actuar
items.description: Termina el cuento o la última nana y llega el momento de apagar la luz. Cuando los padres se disponen a salir de la habitación, una vocecita o un llanto los detiene. A veces basta con sentarse al borde de la cama, dar la mano o dejar la puerta entreabierta. Otras, la despedida se alarga y, horas después, unos pequeños pasos por el pasillo o una llamada desde la cuna vuelven a reclamar su presencia. También hay niños que, después de meses o incluso años durmiendo de manera autónoma, vuelven a necesitar compañía para irse a dormir. Una situación que reabre uno de los debates más recurrentes de la crianza: hasta dónde acompañar, cuándo favorecer que los niños duerman solos y si atender sus demandas es darles seguridad o protegerlos demasiado. ¿Qué hay detrás de esa necesidad de tener cerca a sus padres cuando llega la noche? ¿ Es miedo, costumbre o una forma de buscar seguridad ? ¿Cuándo conviene preocuparse? Seguir leyendo

items.title: La angustia económica revoluciona a los jóvenes: la Gran Insatisfacción recorre Europa
items.description: Europa está siendo atacada militarmente por Rusia , económicamente por China y políticamente por Estados Unidos . Pero los mayores líos están en casa, con un arreón formidable de protestas callejeras que tiene patas arriba al continente más grande y más pequeño, más antiguo y más nuevo, más unido y más dividido del mundo. Y con un superaño electoral por delante (España, Polonia, Italia y la guinda, Francia, junto con varios países más), que examinará cómo digiere ese malestar la vieja democracia liberal. Los jóvenes expresan su frustración en manifestaciones masivas. Los ciudadanos reclaman seguridad, servicios públicos, un refuerzo del poder adquisitivo y cada vez más control de la inmigración. La política no termina de atender esas demandas, y tanto en Bruselas como en los gobiernos nacionales el centro se desmorona . La pujanza de la extrema derecha parece irresistible. La Gran Recesión sacó ese fantasma del armario ropero de la historia: los ultras pasaron entonces de la anécdota a la categoría, pero solo en un puñado de países y con apoyos titubeantes. Aquella crisis nunca se fue del todo: ha dejado algo parecido a una Gran Insatisfacción entre los jóvenes, y una suerte de angustia socioeconómica en todos los demás. La extrema derecha se ha ido asentando en ese lecho fértil para sus propuestas: los ultras alcanzan ya apoyos del 30%, en algunos países incluso más. Y a día de hoy esa marea extremista convive con otro viejo conocido de Europa, las protestas callejeras, a veces incluso violentas, protagonizadas por jóvenes en media docena de países. items.title: Consumer firms defy economic headwinds
items.description: KARACHI: Amid rising food inflation and weakening purchasing power from higher fuel costs driven by Middle East tensions since the start of the US-Israel war on Iran on Feb 28, local and multinational consumer goods companies in Pakistan reported improved sales in the first nine months of 2026 and the first quarter of FY27. However, some companies remain cautious about their full-year 2026 outlook amid persistent inflationary pressures. Nestlé Pakistan Nestlé Pakistan’s net sales for the nine months ended Sept 30, amounted to Rs160bn, up 6.3pc from the corresponding period last year. Despite rising inflation, political instability and higher fuel and energy prices amid the US-Iran war, the company sustained its business momentum. It attributed its performance to increased investment in brands, product innovation and renovation (I&R), stronger marketplace execution, improved export channels and disciplined pricing, where necessary. Local and multinational companies post robust sales growth this year Net profit after tax rose 3.1pc to Rs14.526bn from Rs14.1bn a year earlier, despite higher tax expenses. In response to geopolitical uncertainty, the company accelerated localisation and secured essential inventories to reduce foreign exchange exposure, strengthen supply chain resilience and ensure uninterrupted operations. Citing geopolitical instability, volatile energy and input costs, and persistent inflation, Nestlé maintained a cautious outlook for 2026. FrieslandCampina Engro Pakistan FrieslandCampina Engro Pakistan’s revenue increased 10.1pc to Rs88.4bn in the first nine months of 2026 from Rs80.2bn in the corresponding period last year. The company attributed the growth to a favourable product mix, stronger market execution and selective investment in brands. Profit rose to Rs6.5bn from Rs2bn a year earlier. Regional conflicts, higher freight and energy prices put pressure on the company’s operations and input costs during the third quarter of 2026. In Pakistan, inflation and interest rates also constrained household purchasing power, affecting product affordability and demand, the company said. Unilever Pakistan Unilever Pakistan Foods’ sales rose to Rs37.6bn in the first nine months of 2026 from Rs30bn a year earlier, while profit after tax increased to Rs6.326bn from Rs4.6bn. Unilever said Pakistan’s economy remained resilient, supported by higher foreign exchange reserves, fiscal consolidation and a gradual recovery in economic activity. However, renewed inflation, higher global commodity and energy prices, and Middle East tensions continued to constrain consumer spending, the company added. Colgate-Palmolive Pakistan Colgate-Palmolive Pakistan’s sales rose 25.53pc to Rs52.7bn in July-September 2026, driven by higher prices and sales volumes. Profit after tax increased 8pc to Rs4.9bn compared with the corresponding period last year. The company said persistent inflation, tax collection constraints and high energy tariffs continued to pose challenges. Regional tensions also posed supply chain risks because of its reliance on Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries for essential raw materials. Fauji Foods Fauji Foods Limited (FFL) recorded its highest-ever nine-month revenue of Rs23.9bn in 2026, up 14.1pc from the corresponding period last year. However, profit after tax fell to Rs666m from Rs945m. Despite inflationary pressures on consumption, FFL reported growth across its product portfolio. National Foods Limited National Foods Limited’s sales rose to Rs11.1bn in July-September 2026 from Rs10bn a year earlier, while profit increased to Rs888m from Rs801m. According to Rabia Yousuf of Topline Securities, National Foods informed shareholders at its 55th annual general meeting, held recently, that it expected revenue growth of 15pc in FY27, with scope for further improvement if macroeconomic conditions improved. She said management highlighted a rise in freight rates from $500-$600 to $5,000 per container. Continuing tensions in the Middle East may also constrain export volume growth. Management plans to launch more than 25 products and remains optimistic about expanding its portfolio. Published in Dawn, November 1st, 2026

items.title: India’s water blackmail
items.description: SINCE April 2025, when India unilaterally suspended the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT), most scholarship has treated it as a political decision by the BJP-led NDA government. While it is true that the BJP has been developing a narrative that Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi was ‘rectifying’ the ‘mistakes’ of the Nehruvian era, the decisions and developments during the past 18 months suggest that New Delhi is developing a long-term strategy to strangle Pakistan economically. India’s primary target in this strategic campaign is the Chenab river, which it is systematically converting into a long-term instrument of leverage to dictate Pakistan’s foreign policy, weaken its stance on Kashmir, and dominate bilateral relations. In the 18 months since it decided to keep the IWT in abeyance, India has aggressively leveraged this treaty vacuum to build a massive network of storage, regulation, and diversion infrastructure on the Chenab. New and accelerated hydroelectric power projects, primarily concentrated in the Chenab basin, have ballooned from a baseline capacity of 3,263 MW to 7,620.5 MW, supported by a massive financial outlay of approximately Indian rupees 414.04 billion. No single dam or diversion canal can permanently dry up a river. However, a highly synchronised, connected network of mega structures, coupled with diversion canals, can fundamentally determine who controls the timing and volume of river flow. India is trying to apply a two-pronged strategy, ie, increase storage capacity and enhance the ability to divert the Chenab’s water. India’s strategic roadmap involves five megaprojects alongside extensive local diversions. This includes Sawalkot (1,856 MW), Kirthai I & II (1,320 MW), Pakal Dul (1,000 MW), Ratle (850 MW), and Bursar Storage (800 MW). India’s infrastructure push began in May 2025, with the announcement of the tender for the Uri-II project (240 MW), followed quickly in June 2025 by the tender announcement for the Dulhasti-II project (260 MW). Activity accelerated in July 2025 with two major announcements — first, a tender for the removal of deposited sediments from the Salal Dam Reservoir, and second, the Sawalkot project (1,856 MW) tender under international competitive bidding. In March 2026, civil contracts were officially awarded for both the Uri-I stage II and Dulhasti stage-II projects, alongside the official tender announcement for the highly controversial Chenab-Beas Link Tunnel Project (Link-3). These aforementioned projects command a combined potential diversion and storage capacity of roughly 7.287 MAF. For years, New Delhi has strategically used international platforms and institutional levers to weaken Pakistan’s economic foundations. The Chenab-Beas Link Project is particularly consequential. With a reported budget of Indian rupees 23.52bn, it proposes to transfer water from the Chandra river, a major Chenab tributary, through an 8.7-kilometre tunnel into the Beas basin and onward through a 113km canal network to eastern Indian states. The proposed diversion of 1.9 MAF annually from the Chenab basin raises serious questions about compliance with Article III of the IWT. The threat of manipulation, or the Chenab’s vulnerabilities, poses a direct risk to Pakistan’s economic survival, social stability, and national security. The Chenab directly irrigates agricultural lands across more than 11 districts of central Punjab, the country’s undisputed food basket. These districts form the densest core of the famous rice-wheat cropping zone. This 11-district area accounts for about 22 to 25 per cent of Pakistan’s national food grain output. If India controls water flows during October to December or May to July, it may affect seasonal yields in this zone. In such a scenario, it could cause a direct blow of $9bn to $11bn to Pakistan’s economy. The broader impact would ripple through the national economy in several ways. Pakistan would be forced to spend billions of scarce foreign exchange reserves to import basic food commodities. Instead of generating $3.3bn to $4bn from booming rice exports, the country would face a multibillion-dollar trade deficit just trying to secure alternative grain imports. Second, any sustained restriction on, or unpredictable disruption to, these water flows would threaten the livelihoods of millions of farming households, while endangering crops and compromising national food security. Therefore, Islamabad must view India’s decision to place the IWT in abeyance as another dimension of New Delhi’s long-standing and coordinated policy of economic strangulation of Pakistan. For years, New Delhi has strategically used international platforms and institutional levers to weaken Pakistan’s economic foundations. New Delhi has been consistently trying to restrict Islamabad’s access to global capital and limit its trade capacity. A primary example is India’s aggressive lobbying within the Financial Action Task Force, where it has consistently tried to politicise technical compliance and block Pakistan’s removal from the grey list to discourage foreign direct investment and cripple its banking sector. Beyond regulatory warfare, India has systematically disrupted regional trade platforms, such as Saarc, effectively stalling economic integration across South Asia to keep Pakistan regionally isolated. Faced with this asymmetric threat, Islamabad’s response has been largely concentrated on the external front. Pakistan’s state apparatus has consistently pursued international legal and diplomatic channels. However, a dangerous policy gap exists on the domestic front. Ground-level preparedness is profoundly lacking. The agrarian communities, provincial irrigation departments, and economic sectors that will bear the immediate impact of India’s upstream infrastructure remain highly vulnerable. Pakistan lacks the modern water-storage infrastructure, optimised canal lining, crop-switching strategies, and real-time early warning systems needed to survive sudden changes in river flows. Hence, Islamabad should complement its legal and diplomatic efforts with urgent domestic reforms. Pakistan must declare a national water emergency, educate vulnerable communities in 11 districts of central Punjab that depend on the Chenab, expedite dam construction, and modernise irrigation. Without urgent preparedness, Islamabad will risk surrendering its agricultural security to Delhi’s water blackmail. The writer is a strategic analyst of international security. The views expressed are his own. Published in Dawn, November 1st, 2026

items.title: Uncertain local governments
items.description: THE battle between the Election Commission of Pakistan and the provincial and federal governments has been an almost permanent feature of Pakistan’s electoral scene since 2010, when the responsibility for holding local government elections was entrusted to the Commission under the 18th Amendment. Currently, the ECP is fighting a four-way battle — with the provincial governments of Punjab and KP, the federal government, and the cantonment boards — for LG elections in the two provinces, Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT), and the cantonment boards. The LGs in Sindh and Balochistan (except in the largest district of Quetta, where the entire term passed without election) have yet to complete their terms. The ICT LG election is the most disappointing case. The last LG election in ICT was held in November 2015. Its five-year term ended on Feb 14, 2021. Under the Elections Act, 2017, the new election was to take place within 120 days after the previous LGs’ term ended, making June 15, 2021, the due date for the next election. For more than five years, the ECP and the federal government have been haggling over legal points and the possible date of the next election. Since 2021, the ECP has issued the election schedule four times and carried out fresh delimitation five times. Each time it has had to eat humble pie by withdrawing the schedule as the federal government changed the goalposts and amended the LG election law. The latest in the series was the ICT Local Government (Amendment) Ordinance, 2026, promulgated on Jan 10, 2026, which drastically changed the capital’s LG system. However, the ordinance lapsed in September 2026. While parliament is going through the motions of converting the lapsed ordinance into an act of parliament, the ECP maintains that the old ICTLGA, 2015, stands resurrected after the ordinance lapsed and, therefore, issued a polling schedule on Oct 25, fixing Dec 20 as polling day. Looking back at the federal government’s track record, the new act is likely to pass in the next few days, after which the ECP would have no choice but to withdraw the schedule and begin preparations anew. The case of KP is not very different; the terms of the LGs expired on June 19, 2026, after which new elections should have taken place by Oct 20, but the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Local Government (Amendment) Act, 2026,was passedand became effective on July 16 this year. It changed the size of the village and neighbourhood councils. The ECP strongly objected to the amendment, termed it a delaying tactic, and asked the provincial government to review the law. In the meantime, the ECP is proceeding with preparations to hold the LG polls, except in 12 districts where the law and order situation doesn’t permit polls. The ECP has yet to issue an election schedule. Still, it remains to be seen whether the National Assembly, which has the legislative powers of the KP Assembly after the proclamation of emergency, will amend the LG law or whether the elections will be postponed yet again on some pretext or the other. The ECP is battling both the federal and provincial governments that are reluctant to hold LG polls. All formalities for holding the LG election in Punjab have been completed by the ECP and the Punjab government under the Punjab Local Government Act, 2025. If finally held, this will be the first LG election in roughly 11 years. The election was supposed to be held in May 2022, but a series of new laws and amendments kept postponing it. Although the Punjab government ministerial committee and the ECP agreed to hold the election in three phases between Dec 15 and Jan 15, the Punjab government changed its mind and asked the ECP to defer the election until April 2027 because of dense fog and school exams in December. The ECP immediately rejected the new dates and asked its secretariat to prepare an election schedule based on the earlier agreed dates. The election schedule has not yet been issued; one should wait to see which side blinks first. The election to 43 cantonment boards in the country was due on Aug 8 as the four-year term of the previously elected boards expired on April 11, 2026. The cantonment boards’ election has an additional prerequisite: the ECP should receive the federal government’s request before holding the election. Reportedly, no such request has been received, and the ECP, given the legal requirement to hold elections within 120 days of the expiry of the term, is trying to reach out to the federal government. Regardless of the outcome of these efforts, the election to the cantonment boards is also overdue. These four stories lead to a single conclusion: both the federal and provincial governments are reluctant to hold LG elections on one pretext or another. The key flaw in the system is that while the ECP is responsible for holding LG elections, the governments and their legislatures alone write the LG laws. There is no bar on legislatures amending LG laws. As demonstrated repeatedly, the law can be amended after the announcement of the election schedule and even a few days before polling day, undoing all the preparation made by the ECP such as delimiting LG boundaries. The solution is for parliament to amend the Elections Act, 2017, and bar any amendment to the LG laws after the expiry of the LG term, so the ECP can prepare unimpeded and hold timely elections. As if these difficulties were not enough to make the future of LGs uncertain, another layer of unpredictability has been added by the possibility of carving out new provinces and, in the case of ICT, by the announcement that Islamabad may soon have provincial status. This may give the government yet another pretext to slow-walk LG elections. The writer is the president of Pakistan-based think tank Pildat.president@pildat.org X: @ABMPildat Published in Dawn, November 1st, 2026

items.title: Is the NPP orchestrating an undemocratic power grab to shield incumbent MPs ahead of 2028?
items.description: The New Patriotic Party (NPP), historically revered as a bastion of intra-party democracy and constitutional governance in Ghana, appears to be executing a retrograde maneuver. As the party prepares to select its parliamentary standard-bearers for the crucial 2028 General Elections, its leadership seems intent on compromising the very values and foundational tenets that once defined its identity. Rather than adhering to the time-tested, egalitarian tradition of opening nominations to all qualified aspirants, the party leadership, via recent official circulars and a press conference convened by the General Secretary, is introducing a dubious, unprecedented political experiment. While dynamic change and innovation are vital features of organizational growth, novel mechanisms must be approached with utmost prudence. Political wisdom dictates a simple truth: you do not reinvent the wheel when nothing is broken. Mechanics of Exclusion: To fully understand the gravity of the current tension, one must examine the backdrop of the NPP’s recent history. Following a bruising defeat in the 2024 General Elections, the party found itself stripped of its parliamentary majority, reduced to a fragile minority caucus of just 87 Members of Parliament (MPs). Rather than undergoing genuine introspective reform and rebuilding grassroots confidence, the newly minted national executive committee, spearheaded by National Chairman John Boadu, has instead embarked on a heavy-handed, bureaucratic strategy to insulate incumbents. Under this newly hatched, regimented framework, party members aspiring to contest the upcoming parliamentary primaries are subjected to a draconian multi-tiered barrier. Pre-Declaration of Intent: Aspirants must first submit a formal application of intent to the party’s central secretariat. Bureaucratic Vetting: Aspirants must undergo mandatory vetting before they are even permitted to actively campaign or engage delegates. Mandatory Orientation & Assessment: Those vetted must attend a party-run academy to undergo political “orientation” and an arbitrary suitability evaluation. To characterize this cumbersome and exclusionary process as anything short of unthinkable, autocratic, and deeply anti-democratic would be an understatement. [Traditional Open Nomination Process] └──> Equal access to all qualified aspirants ──> Grassroots Delegate Vote [Proposed 2028 Bureaucratic Framework] └──> Intent Screening ──> Pre-Vetting ──> Academy Assessment ──> Handpicked Incumbent Protection Incumbent Protection: Under Article 94 of the 1992 Constitution of Ghana, any citizen of sound mind, appropriate age, and without a criminal record possesses the fundamental right to seek parliamentary office. Why, then, is the NPP hierarchy manufacturing such ludicrous, coercive, and bureaucratic hurdles? The overarching objective is transparent and it is to engineer a slate of unopposed candidates and shield the 87 incumbent MPs from democratic accountability. This protective posture raises fundamental questions about performance and merit. Where is the Accountability? If incumbent MPs have served dutifully, honored their pledges, and aligned with the aspirations of their constituencies, why shield them from democratic contestation? What Legacy Are We Protecting? Beyond posturing on legislative issues and engaging in partisan walkouts, what extraordinary legislative triumphs have these 87 MPs achieved to warrant automatic protection? Danger of Entitlement: Shielding lawmakers from primary battles rewards complacency and insulates them from the very constituents they were elected to serve. If the national leadership genuinely believes that protecting incumbents serves the party’s strategic interest, it should state so forthrightly and debate the matter openly, rather than erecting insidious administrative barriers designed to disqualify challengers by stealth. Political Backlash The national executive body must recognize that it cannot arbitrarily disenfranchise party loyalists who fulfill the constitutional and statutory requirements to contest elections. By persisting with this archaic, regimented, and deeply flawed scheme ahead of the nomination window scheduled for November 1 to November 10, 2026, the party is practically inviting a destructive avalanche of litigation. Furthermore, this heavy-handed approach ignores the political maturity of the NPP’s core constituency. NPP delegates across the country’s 275 constituencies have repeatedly demonstrated sound judgment, political discernment, and tactical wisdom at the ballot box. Attempting to headhunt candidates or impose incumbents top-down grossly underestimates the intelligence of the grassroots base. “A stitch in time saves nine. Attempting to bypass the delegates’ democratic mandate will not consolidate power, it will shatter the party’s foundation.” Democratic Integrity: The NPP leadership stands at a critical crossroads. The ill-conceived strategy to gag aspirants and coddle incumbents will inevitably ignite widespread apathy, bitter factionalism, and irreparable fissures across its electoral base. The grassroots membership of the NPP remains far too discerning to accept dictated outcomes from national officers who hold office by virtue of temporary privilege. The party executive must immediately shelve this backward, autocratic ploy and restore an open, transparent, and unhindered primary process. If the system is not broken, the NPP must refrain from destructive tinkering. Let the delegates decide!

items.title: Islamabad High Court bars FIR mention in character certificates after acquittal
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The Islamabad High Court (IHC) has ruled that police cannot mention an FIR in the character certificate of a citizen who has been acquitted in the case, declaring any such certificate unlawful and invalid. Justice Ayyaz Shaukat, while deciding a public interest petition, directed the Inspector General of Police, Islamabad, to establish a formal mechanism to ensure that references to criminal cases ending in acquittal are not included in character certificates issued to citizens. The court observed that citizens should not be compelled to approach courts to exercise rights already guaranteed under the law. It held that following an acquittal, there was no legal justification for portraying an individual as an accused or criminal through a police-issued character certificate. Rules such mention violates constitutional rights, including dignity and freedom of movement Allowing the petition, the court ordered the removal of a reference to an FIR registered at Shalimar Police Station from the petitioner’s character certificate. The judgement clarified that although police could maintain internal records of criminal cases for official purposes, such information could not be disclosed in character certificates issued to citizens, particularly when these were required for travelling abroad. It further observed that there was no legal basis for mentioning an FIR in a character certificate after the proceedings had culminated in a final acquittal. Any certificate containing such a reference would be legally invalid. Justice Ayyaz Shaukat also rejected the police’s description of the petitioner as having been “discharged” during the investigation, observing that such a characterisation undermined the legal effect and status of the acquittal. The court held that including an FIR in a character certificate despite an individual’s acquittal violated Articles 4, 9, 14 and 15 of the Constitution, which protect citizens’ rights, liberty, dignity and freedom of movement. It emphasised that a person acquitted through due process of law could not continue to face adverse consequences through a character certificate suggesting involvement in criminal proceedings. The court directed the Islamabad police chief to introduce a proper procedure to ensure that acquitted citizens did not have to initiate fresh litigation merely to obtain character certificates reflecting their actual legal status. Published in Dawn, November 1st, 2026

items.title: From engineering to the pulpit: Prophet Jimmy marks 20 years in prophetic ministry
items.description: Before becoming known as Prophet Jimmy, Jimmy Alla-Mensah had built a professional career in network and security engineering, working with major organisations including Verizon and Lockheed Martin. He had invested years in education, professional development and technical certifications, particularly in Cisco networking and security. It was a career path that offered professional fulfilment and a future he believed he could predict. But in November 2006, he made a decision that would take his life in a direction he had not originally planned: entering prophetic ministry. For the US-based Ghanaian prophet, the transition was not the result of a failed career or a lack of professional opportunities. Rather, he says, it followed a growing conviction that God had a different assignment for his life. His spiritual journey had taken a significant turn on April 14, 2004, when he became born again. As his relationship with God developed, he says, so did his understanding of purpose. By November 2006, he had stepped into prophetic ministry, leaving behind the relative familiarity of the engineering profession for a calling that presented an entirely different set of demands. A different kind of preparation The transition was particularly significant because, unlike his engineering career, prophetic ministry was not something he had spent years studying or preparing for professionally. Prophet Jimmy says he entered ministry without formal prophetic training, prior ministry experience or the opportunity to understudy an experienced minister. He therefore had to learn while carrying the responsibilities of ministry, depending on prayer, Scripture study, personal discipline and experience. The experience, he says, taught him that having a calling does not automatically mean one has developed the maturity required to fulfil it. “Anointing does not eliminate the need for wisdom. A calling does not remove the need for character. And spiritual gifts do not exempt anyone from learning,” he reflects. His experience has also strengthened his appreciation for mentorship, accountability and sound biblical foundations. Beyond professional fulfilment The demands of ministry have also introduced him to challenges quite different from those he encountered in engineering. Where his previous profession involved network infrastructure, security systems and technical solutions, ministry has brought him into direct contact with people dealing with sickness, broken relationships, financial difficulties, hopelessness and spiritual struggles. He speaks of nights spent in prayer, long counselling hours, emotional exhaustion, disappointments and the responsibility of standing with people through difficult moments. Yet, he says, the opportunity to see people regain hope and find strength has given the work a different kind of meaning. “My engineering career gave me professional fulfillment. Ministry has given me the opportunity to participate in something that reaches deeply into the lives of people,” he says. He acknowledges that the joy of serving comes with sacrifices, but says he remains grateful for the privilege of serving God and people. Twenty years of a different journey The journey has not been without difficult seasons. One particularly painful experience was watching a church he had worked hard to build decline from approximately 300 congregants to about 10. The experience brought questions about failure, purpose and whether he had the strength to continue. It also taught him not to measure the success of a calling solely by attendance, popularity or public recognition. Looking back, he says he would tell his younger self to remain humble, learn from mistakes, care for his health and protect his family. He would also remind himself that ministers are human beings who sometimes need encouragement and rest. “Above all, remember that you are a human being before you are a minister,” he says. As he prepares to mark 20 years in prophetic ministry, Prophet Jimmy describes the journey as one that has tested his faith, challenged his assumptions and reshaped his understanding of leadership and service. The anniversary celebration is scheduled for Sunday, November 8, 2026, at House of Divine Glory Ministry International, 7895 Cessna Avenue, Suite B, Gaithersburg, Maryland 20879. The celebration will reflect the themes of “20 Years of Grace,” “20 Years of Ministry” and “20 Years of God’s Faithfulness.” For Prophet Jimmy, the words of 1 Samuel 7:12 capture the significance of the milestone: “HITHERTO HATH THE LORD HELPED US.”

items.title: US to deport 150 Afghan immigrants back to Kabul
items.description: WASHINGTON: President Don­­ald Trump’s administration plans to deport more than 150 Afghan immigrants back to Afghanistan via Pakistan, US media reported, a move advocacy groups say could endanger their lives. Trump last year issued travel bans for a number of countries, including Afghanistan, as part of a broad immigration crackdown, and sought to end deportation protections for Afghans, some of whom were granted special immigrant visas following the August 2021 takeover by the Taliban. More than 150 Afghan immigrants are expected to be deported in the latest push, The New York Times reported on Friday, citing three unnamed US officials, and the first flight could leave as soon as Monday. Among those expected to be deported are relatives of Afghans who assisted the US military in the country prior to the fall of Kabul, according to AfghanEvac, a group seeking to help former Afghan allies. While the US cannot arrange deportations directly to Afgha­n­istan, the officials told the Times that Pakistan will oversee their expulsion to Afghanistan. Published in Dawn, November 1st, 2026

items.title: LPG price twice the official rate in open market
items.description: • Ogra notifies about Rs15 per kg increase in gas price • Association warns of strike from Nov 16 over new LPG policy ISLAMABAD: As the government again notified an increase in the price of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) for November, its price in the open market is twice as high as the official rate amid a shortage of LPG due to the US-Iran war. In a notification on Saturday, the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) notified Rs294,075 per tonne for November compared to Rs279,341 in the previous month. Following the increase, the official retail rate of an 11.8 kg domestic cylinder of LPG is Rs3,470, up by Rs173. The official LPG rate is Rs294 per kilogramme. The oil and gas regulator said that the LPG producer price was linked with Saudi Aramco-CP and the US dollar exchange rate. It added that compared to the previous month, Saudi Aramco-CP had increased by 6.47 per cent, while the average dollar exchange rate had slightly decreased by 0.12pc, resulting in an increase in the LPG consumer price by Rs14.73 per kg. In the open market, LPG is selling for up to Rs630 per kg, while the company-operated franchises are charging up to Rs400 per kg, with many warning that the crisis would compound due to the gas shortage. LPG Distributors Association of Pakistan Chairman Irfan Khokhar said that the situation was serious because of the Iran border closure . He said at least 70 per cent of LPG was imported from Iran, while only 30pc was locally produced. “The government has to make serious efforts to control market manipulations,” Mr Khokhar added. On the other hand, LPG marketing companies thre­atened to shut down their businesses from Nov 16 if the private sector was sidelined in the upcoming LPG policy. Pakistan LPG Marketers Association Cha­irman Ali Haider warned that they will observe a strike from Nov 16 if the government implemented the policy. He said the government should not reverse the deregulation of LPG, adding that the gas was in short supply due to the Iran border closure. “Out of around 1.3 million tonnes, only around 225,000 is imported from the Gulf, and that too has been mainly imported by the private sector,” he said, adding that the ProGas terminal at Port Qasim was under the control of the Sui Southern Gas Company which “imported LPG around seven months back”. The association also wrote a letter to Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik, stating the draft policy sent to the prime minister had no input from the private sector. The association called for the complete deregulation of the LPG sector. It said the 2016 LPG policy imposed Rs4,669 per tonne petroleum development levy on locally produced LPG. This was imposed to provide subsidies to the state-owned entities such as the PSO, Parco, and SSGC to import LPG during winters and in any emergency, like the current scenario. “Despite billions of rupees collected in terms of PDL through this formula, the state-owned entities have failed to import LPG during these days,” Mr Haider alleged. Published in Dawn, November 1st, 2026

items.title: Iran, Qatar hold talks as Tehran weighs US diplomatic overture
items.description: Iranian and Qatari officials reportedly held talks over the weekend on proposals to end the conflict with the United States, as Tehran reviewed a US diplomatic overture but said it had no immediate plans for direct negotiations with Washington. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Saturday that Tehran would decide whether to hold direct or indirect talks only after Washington agreed to its conditions. In an interview with Al Jazeera, Araghchi described a recent US effort to reopen dialogue as a positive step but dismissed reports of an imminent meeting between the two sides as speculation. Iranian negotiators met Qatari mediators in Doha on Saturday, following more than 12 hours of discussions between Iranian and Qatari envoys in Tehran on Friday, Reuters reported, citing a source. The talks were being coordinated through regular contacts with Washington. Araghchi said Iran's demands included the lifting of sanctions imposed after the Islamabad memorandum of understanding, the restoration of waivers for Iranian oil exports, the release of frozen Iranian assets and a reduction in US military forces in the region. Tehran also wanted an end to hostilities on all fronts, including Lebanon. On the Strait of Hormuz, Araghchi said Iran had reached agreement with mediators on a new proposal that could allow the waterway to be fully reopened within two days. Tehran also wants Washington to recognize a new shipping route developed with Oman, while other routes through the strait would be closed. The diplomatic efforts follow a letter from US Vice President JD Vance to Iran's security chief, Mohsen Rezaei, delivered through Qatari mediators. US media reports said the letter proposed direct negotiations led by Vance, with Iran's nuclear program on the agenda from the outset. Rezaei said the tone of the letter marked a significant shift in Washington's approach. He also said Iran was debating whether to abandon its longstanding ban on nuclear weapons if fighting resumed, although no decision had been made. The diplomatic contacts have done little to ease concerns about a return to fighting. Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei warned on Saturday that any new US or Israeli attack would be met with an immediate response without geographical restrictions. Iran's military later said it was taking steps to strengthen its readiness. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Trump had not decided whether to resume military action, adding that Washington preferred a diplomatic solution but was prepared to act if necessary. Trump, who launched the war alongside Israel on February 28, said on Friday that the conflict would end "very soon" but gave no details. Regional countries have been concerned that Washington could resume attacks after the US midterm elections. (Cover: A visitor to the Museum of Islamic Art takes pictures of the skyline of high-rise buildings in Doha on July 9, 2026. /VCG)

items.title: SMOKERS’ CORNER: THE MYTH OF PTI’S POPULARITY
items.description: For years, political analysts across the board, from pro-Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf (PTI) commentators to supposedly neutral and anti-PTI observers, insisted that PTI was the most popular political party in the country. This narrative was even widely echoed by Western media outlets. Lately, however, that conviction has eroded. Commentators first began backtracking by limiting their claims about PTI’s dominance to Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP), but even that has started to falter. What many mistook for widespread support may simply have been what political scientists refer to as “manufactured popularity.” Manufactured popularity is not a reflection of unmediated public sentiment. Instead, it is a carefully crafted construct accumulated through symbolic engineering, media management, state or institutional sponsorship, and the strategic exploitation of public disillusionment. At its core, manufactured popularity depends on presenting a leader as a spotless saviour, who is capable of dismantling a ‘corrupt’ old order. This form of popularity is built on exaggerated promises and carefully curated media narratives. But the moment an engineered project makes the transition from opposition to executive power, tensions between rhetoric and governance begin to dissolve the illusion. Throughout history, political regimes and movements have demonstrated how manufactured popularity can decay when confronted with cold realities. In the 1950s, former president Juan Perón’s initial popularity in Argentina was sustained by heavy state subsidies and nationalistic appeals. Yet, as economic historian Carlos Díaz-Alejandro documented in his analyses of Argentine economic history, the regime’s inability to sustain fiscal extravagance amidst soaring inflation and foreign exchange depletion eventually caused Perón’s populist economic model to unravel, hastening widespread unrest and military intervention. While PTI’s online dominance is often taken as proof of overwhelming public support, digital visibility, electoral success and the ability to mobilise people on the streets are three very different measures of political strength In post-communist Eastern Europe, the rise and fall of political movements that relied on media-driven anti-corruption narratives, such as Simeon Saxe-Coburg-Gotha’s movement in Bulgaria during the early 2000s, illustrate that popularity constructed primarily on outsider status and high moral claims quickly evaporates when administrative ineptitude and economic compromises take hold in daily governance. PTI, formed by Imran Khan in 1996, is an intriguing example. It remained a minor player on the margins of Pakistani politics till its transformation into a dominant force in 2011. The transformation was not merely an ‘awakening’ but also a carefully constructed political phenomenon. PTI’s popularity was methodically cultivated, mainly by the military establishment. Indeed, the party effectively mobilised a real sense of grievance among urban middle-class voters who were exhausted by the perceived ‘corruption’ of traditional parties such as the Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) and the Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP). But this was amplified by institutional engineering through a hybrid scheme. According to the Pakistani political scholar Muhammad Waseem, in this scheme, intelligence agencies steered the media narrative, weakened political opponents, and directed influential political “electables” towards PTI. Illustration by Abro The architecture of PTI’s popularity was heavily built on a modern communication strategy. According to the media researcher Ifrah Nadeem, PTI pioneered the use of “computational propaganda.” It unleashed tightly targeted social media campaigns, and emotional messaging. By leveraging digital spaces, the party bypassed mainstream journalistic scrutiny, portraying Khan as an incorruptible reformer who alone could usher in a ‘Naya [New] Pakistan.’ According to economists such as Atif Mian and academic assessments by the International Crisis Group, governing a state such as Pakistan that is under severe balance-of-payments distress required unpopular policy adjustments. But this contradicted PTI’s idealised campaign claims. So, when Khan was placed in power in 2018, the election of an ‘honest leader’ was framed by the party as a good enough condition for economic revival and institutional purification. But Khan blundered his way across almost all vital areas of governance. This resulted in the gradual pullback of the military establishment’s patronage of his regime. Therefore, the manufactured framework sustaining the government collapsed, culminating in Khan’s removal via a constitutional vote of no-confidence in 2022. The erosion of manufactured popularity reveals a recurring dynamic in politics. According to the American political scientist Samuel P. Huntington, while media manipulation, emotional appeals and institutional patronage can create an impression of overwhelming public approval, they cannot transform into tangible administrative competence and economic stability. While failing leaders who were elevated through manufactured popularity often switch to narratives of victimisation or conspiracy to retain a dedicated core, the initial perception of popularity begins to alter when tested by on-ground political realities. But here’s the interesting bit: even after Khan’s fall, the narrative of his ‘popularity’ did not recede as such. At least not in the media. Political commentators and international monitoring groups viewed the support for PTI-backed candidates in the 2024 general elections as proof of this. However, one can posit that this was largely achieved through PTI’s formal and informal social media apparatus transitioning the party’s narrative from that of producing an incorruptible saviour to one of moral victimisation. In the aftermath of Khan’s arrest in 2023, PTI’s media apparatus cleverly converted the general public anger over rising inflation and political instability (which Khan’s regime left behind), into an unquestioning loyalty to the imprisoned Khan. This was further reinforced by digital algorithms that amplified symbolic/performative acts of resistance, creating an impression of impressive public mobilisation. However, the eventual reality check occurred when the limits of this online and sentiment-based popularity were tested on the ground. The definitive moment arrived when the current coalition government-imposed emergency measures and governor’s rule in KP recently, sidelining PTI’s provincial government there. Contrary to expectations of an uprising, the public response was muted. The failure of the party to mobilise street demonstrations underscored a disconnect between online sentiment and real-life capacity. This led political analysts to re-evaluate the nature of the party’s popular base. They began recognising that much of what had been interpreted as deep political commitment was, in fact, passive sympathy, digital noise, and an anti-establishment protest vote rather than an organised, resilient political movement. The illusion of overwhelming popularity unravels when passive sympathisers who express support on social media or through voting, decline to transform into active political actors on the streets. They are in the majority, and many are even stationed abroad. The loss of PTI’s last institutional foothold in KP demonstrates that, while manufactured popularity and grievance-based narratives can maintain an electoral pull, they remain inherently fragile when confronted with state power, and the reality of growing public apathy. The electoral pull too is now likely to recede, especially with the likelihood of Khan remaining behind bars in the foreseeable future. Published in Dawn, EOS, November 1st, 2026

items.title: ‘Medicine pricing needs serious attention’
items.description: KARACHI: More than 86,000 medicines produced by pharmaceutical companies have been registered under the Track and Trace System, allowing consumers to scan products by mobile phone to check their authenticity and find out their prices, Federal Health Minister Mustafa Kamal said. He said that pharmaceutical companies could also register their medicines and products online. A process that previously took years is now being completed within just 21 days. Addressing the members of the Korangi Association of Trade and Industry (KATI) on Saturday, he said the Drug Regulatory Authority of Pakistan (DRAP) has been made fully transparent and digitalised. Eight months had passed since DRAP’s certification procedures were shifted to a digital system, during which more than 5,000 cases had been processed, he said. Mustafa Kamal said the issue of medicine pricing requires serious attention. The pharmaceutical industries seek an increase in medicine prices, but the matter is under consideration by the federal cabinet. The issue has two dimensions as an increase in medicine prices will create additional financial difficulties for ordinary citizens, while keeping prices unchanged could lead to shortages of medicines for serious illnesses. Consequently, patients were sometimes forced to purchase the same medicines from the black market at three times their actual price. Published in Dawn, November 1st, 2026

items.title: Nuclear science boosts Pakistan’s ability to track groundwater
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Pakistan has strengthened its ability to track groundwater resources using nuclear science, enabling scientists to identify recharge sources, determine groundwater age and trace contamination pathways, according to an International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) report released on Saturday. The Regional Cooperative Agree­ment (RCA) for Research, Deve­lopment and Training Related to Nuclear Science and Technology for Asia and the Pacific, Hydrology and Groundwater programme has significantly enhanced Pakistan’s capacity for continuous groundwater monitoring through the application of isotope-based techniques. This advancement has considerably strengthened the connection between scientific research and water governance, allowing for more precise and systematic observation of groundwater dynamics across diverse hydrogeological settings, the IAEA report said. Studies undertaken through RCA-supported projects have generated reliable estimates of groundwater recharge rates, aquifer interconnections and pollution pathways in key regions such as the Indus Plain, the Quetta Valley and the Cholistan Desert. IAEA report says RCA-backed isotope techniques help country trace water sources, age, pollution pathways These findings have deepened the scientific understanding of Pakistan’s groundwater systems while providing essential inputs for developing long-term strategies for water reso­urce management, the agency noted. Prior to joining the programme, groundwater monitoring was not a primary focus of national hydrological investigations. Several studies were conducted using conventional methods, such as hydro-chemical analyses and physical measurements, but these approaches provided only basic information on water table depth, water quality and aquifer dynamics. Through its participation in the programme, Pakistan has significantly strengthened its laboratory capacity for isotope hydrology. The Pakistan Institute of Nuclear Science and Technology (Pinstech) now hosts one of the region’s most advanced isotope analysis facilities, complemented by 12 laboratories nationwide. Currently, Pinstech and the Pakistan Council of Research in Water Resources work in close collaboration to incorporate isotopic data into national groundwater management models. “This integration supports the early detection of over-extraction, salinity intrusion and other forms of aquifer stress, thereby contributing to more sustainable groundwater utilisation,” the report said. The focus on data-driven management has fostered a stronger culture of evidence-based decision-making within national and provincial water institutions. Policymakers are increasingly rel­ying on isotope hydrology data to inf­orm regulatory frameworks, resource allocation and long-term planning, reflecting a significant shift from reactive to preventive and science-informed groundwater management. Pakistan’s participation has delivered substantial economic, social and environmental benefits. Published in Dawn, November 1st, 2026

items.title: Santé : Le restaurant Miam Diet mobilise la population pour une alimentation saine
items.description: Le Centre culturel du Faso a accueilli, le samedi 31 octobre 2026, la Journée de l'alimentation saine et du bien-être (JASBE), placée sous le thème « Nos produits locaux au service de notre santé ». Dépistages multiples, don de sang, panels et fitness ont rythmé cette journée de sensibilisation, portée par la nutritionniste Danielle Wendyam Laeticia Bouda et placée sous le patronage du ministre d'État en charge de l'Agriculture, Ismaël Sombié. L'événement a réuni plusieurs centaines de participants autour d'un programme résolument tourné vers la prévention. Toute la journée, des stands de dépistage ont permis aux visiteurs de tester leur glycémie (diabète), d'évaluer leur condition physique avec orientation vers le sport adapté, ou encore de se faire dépister pour le cancer du sein et du col de l'utérus. Un espace dédié au don de sang a également été installé, tandis que des panels sur la santé et le bien-être se sont succédé, complétés par des séances de fitness. Porteuse de l'initiative, la nutritionniste bilingue Danielle Wendyam Laeticia Bouda, promotrice du cabinet et restaurant diététique Miam Diet, a rappelé la philosophie qui guide son engagement « Manger sain ne doit ni être une contrainte, ni un luxe » Porteuse de l'initiative, la nutritionniste bilingue Danielle Wendyam Laeticia Bouda, promotrice du cabinet et restaurant diététique Miam Diet, a rappelé la philosophie qui guide son engagement. Une conviction qu'elle résume ainsi : « manger sain ne doit ni être une contrainte, ni un luxe, mais un véritable mode de vie accessible à tous ». Selon elle, les produits locaux burkinabè disposent de tous les atouts pour accompagner cette transition alimentaire, à condition que le public s'en empare. Son cabinet, spécialisé dans la prise en charge des maladies non transmissibles, collabore étroitement avec des médecins, des centres de bien-être et des structures sportives. Le ministre Sombié salue une thématique « pertinente » Représenté par Diakalia Zon à la cérémonie, le ministre d'État, ministre de l'Agriculture, de l'Eau, des Ressources animales et halieutiques, le commandant Ismaël Sombié, a salué la pertinence du thème retenu. Pour le représentant du ministre, la valorisation des produits locaux constitue un levier double : elle soutient la production nationale tout en offrant aux populations une alimentation de qualité, adaptée à leurs besoins nutritionnels. Un aperçu du public Une position constante pour le département, qui a fait de la transformation locale et de la consommation des productions endogènes un axe majeur de sa politique. Les organisateurs entendent faire de cette journée un rendez-vous annuel, afin d'ancrer durablement les réflexes de prévention et de consommation locale dans les habitudes des Ouagalais. Minute.bf

items.title: 2026 Luv FM-Republic Bank Habitat mini-clinic records huge success in Kumasi
items.description: The mini-clinic of the 2026 edition of the Luv FM-Republic Bank Habitat has recorded a successful outing in Kumasi, bringing together key players in Ghana’s housing and construction industry to promote affordable and accessible homeownership. The event, held on October 29, 2026, at the Opoku Trading Arena in Adum, offered prospective homeowners, property developers and industry professionals an opportunity to engage institutions providing housing services, construction materials, financing and interior decoration solutions. Now in its eighth year, the Habitat Fair seeks to address some of the challenges associated with land acquisition, building and homeownership, particularly in the Ashanti Region. Organised in partnership with Republic Bank, the mini-clinic brought together stakeholders across the housing and construction value chain. Visitors had the opportunity to access professional guidance, explore products and services, and consider solutions suited to their housing needs and budgets. Institutions offer guidance on homeownership The Lands Commission and the Asantehene’s Lands Secretariat were among the participating institutions, providing visitors with information and guidance on land-related matters and other aspects of homeownership. The event also showcased construction materials, home improvement products and interior decoration solutions. JetSky Roofing Systems engaged patrons on its fire-resistant roofing systems and window products, while Prestodea Ghana showcased glass windows, balustrades and doors. A representative of the Asantehene’s Lands Secretariat highlighted the importance of the initiative in helping members of the public navigate their homeownership aspirations. Republic Bank highlights mortgage support Head of Mortgage Banking at Republic Bank, Dan Adjetey Mohenu, reaffirmed the bank’s commitment to supporting individuals at different stages of their homeownership journey. He explained that the bank’s mortgage and housing finance solutions were not limited to purchasing completed properties but also catered for individuals who prefer to construct their homes in phases. The financing options, he said, could support different stages of construction, from foundation works to interior decoration, subject to the bank’s assessment criteria and requirements. Main Habitat Fair scheduled for November The partnership between Luv FM and Republic Bank is expected to continue offering prospective homeowners access to financial guidance and other essential services as they work towards owning homes. The mini-clinic serves as a lead-up to the main 2026 Habitat Fair, scheduled to take place from November 25 to 29 in Kumasi. The initiative comes amid growing demand for housing driven by population growth and urbanisation, with organisers positioning the fair as a platform for connecting prospective homeowners with institutions and services across the housing sector.

items.title: Incendies de poteaux électriques : la Somelec met en cause des techniciens externes à la société et des branchements anarchiques et illégaux
items.description: La Société mauritanienne d'électricité « Somelec » a déclaré que le recours à des techniciens grimpeurs non qualifiés et n'appartenant pas à ses équipes officielles, l'utilisation de câbles de mauvaise qualité et le recours à des méthodes de raccordement anarchiques et illégaux étaient à l'origine des incendies récurrents sur les poteaux électriques. La société a ajouté, dans un communiqué publié ce samedi, que ces pratiques provoquent des courts-circuits lorsque les charges et la pression sur le réseau augmentent, ce qui constitue une charge dépassant la capacité des poteaux et des transformateurs. La société a annoncé le lancement d’une campagne sur le terrain visant à supprimer les raccordements illégaux et illégaux, et à régulariser les raccordements sur les poteaux et le réseau électrique de la capitale, Nouakchott. Somelec a appelé les citoyens à contribuer à la protection du réseau électrique et à lutter contre les branchements illégaux, mettant en garde contre les risques qu’ils font peser sur les vies humaines, les biens et la sécurité des quartiers résidentiels. La capitale Nouakchott a récemment connu des incendies à répétition dans des installations électriques, notamment des postes de distribution et des locaux techniques, dont la société « Somelec » a attribué les causes à une surcharge électrique et à la hausse des températures.

items.title: Sénégal : le parlement rejette pour la deuxième fois le budget rectificatif présenté par le gouvernement
items.description: Le Parlement sénégalais a rejeté, pour la deuxième fois, le budget rectificatif pour l'année 2026, une décision qui menace la conclusion d'un nouvel accord de financement avec le Fonds monétaire international d'un montant de 2,2 milliards de dollars. Le parti « Pastef » a déclaré dans un communiqué que ce rejet était motivé par ce qu’il a qualifié de manque de transparence du budget, par l’inefficacité des mesures prises pour lutter contre la hausse du coût de la vie, ainsi que par le refus du gouvernement de fournir des documents essentiels ou de rationaliser les fonds spéciaux. La commission des finances de l’Assemblée nationale (le Parlement) avait annoncé mardi dernier qu’elle réexaminerait le budget rectificatif, après l’avoir rejeté en première lecture. Ce désaccord sur le budget pourrait compromettre les espoirs du Sénégal d’obtenir, dès le début du mois prochain, l’approbation par le conseil d’administration du FMI d’un programme de financement de 2,2 milliards de dollars s’étalant sur trois ans. Le Sénégal est confronté à un endettement atteignant 132 % du produit intérieur brut (PIB) à la fin de l’année 2024, selon les données du Fonds monétaire international. Le budget révisé abaisse les prévisions de croissance du PIB réel pour 2026 à 2,7 %, contre environ 5 %, et porte le déficit budgétaire à 7,6 % du PIB, contre 5,4 % dans les estimations précédentes.

items.title: Le ministre des domaines et du patrimoine de l’état en visite sur les chantiers en cours dans la ville de Zouerate
items.description: Le ministre des domaines, du patrimoine de l'état et de la réforme foncière, Mamoudou Mamadou Niang, a donné des instructions pour accélérer le rythme des travaux de l'hôpital régional en cours de construction dans la ville de Zouerate pour qu’ils puissent s’achever dans les délais fixés, dans le respect des spécifications et des normes techniques requises. Ces instructions ont été données par le ministre lors d’une visite sur le terrain qu’il a effectuée ce samedi dans plusieurs chantiers menés dans le cadre du programme d’urgence visant à généraliser l’accès aux services essentiels au développement local, afin de s’informer de l’avancement des travaux et de l’état de préparation des installations achevées. La visite a concerné des établissements scolaires, notamment l’école «Tarhil 2 », où le ministre a inspecté quatre salles de classe dont les travaux sont achevés, ainsi que l’école « député Saïdou Wane », où les travaux réalisés par la Délégation générale pour la solidarité nationale et la lutte contre l’exclusion « Taazour » ont été menés à bien.
